definition_zh: 令人憎恶的事物；被诅咒的人；革出教门的惩罚
definition_en: something or someone that is intensely disliked or detested; a formal curse by a church
core_image: 被全村人指着的罪人：人人避之唯恐不及
scene: 在那个小镇上，说谎被视为最不可饶恕的恶习。 In that town, lying was anathema to everyone, and no liar was ever trusted again.
sceneCN: 这里的 anathema 是「人人憎恶之事」（第 1 个义项：极其厌恶的东西）；句意是在那个镇上撒谎为人人所不齿，撒谎者再也不会被信任。

pos.zh: 令人憎恶的事物；诅咒；革出教门

derivatives.zh: 由 anathema 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「诅咒；将…革出教门」
由 anathematize 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「诅咒的行为；革出教门」
由 anathema 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「受诅咒的；遭憎恶的」

senses.title: Something intensely detested
senses.definition: a thing or an idea that someone detests strongly, as if it were cursed
senses.definitionCN: 某人极为憎恶、视若诅咒般避之不及的事物或观念
senses.example: Raising taxes is anathema to most voters.
senses.exampleCN: 加税是大多数选民深恶痛绝的事。
senses.why: The churchly curse became a metaphor: whatever is cursed is hated, so the word drifted to any detested thing.
senses.whyCN: 宗教诅咒变成比喻：被诅咒的即是人见人恨的，词义因此泛化到任何令人深恶痛绝的事物。

senses.title: A person who is cursed or detested
senses.titleCN: 被诅咒的人；遭憎恶的人
senses.definition: a person who is cursed or regarded with intense dislike by a group
senses.definitionCN: 被诅咒的、或被某个群体极度厌恶的人
senses.example: The traitor became an anathema to his own family.
senses.exampleCN: 这个叛徒成了连家人都憎恶的人。
senses.why: A curse can fall on people as well as things, so the noun also names the cursed person himself.
senses.whyCN: 诅咒既可以加于物也可以加于人，因此该名词也指那个被诅咒、遭唾弃的人。

senses.title: A formal church curse
senses.definition: a solemn curse pronounced by church authority, especially one that excommunicates a person
senses.definitionCN: 由教会权威郑重宣布的诅咒，尤指将某人逐出教会的惩罚
senses.example: In medieval times, an anathema cut a sinner off from all sacraments.
senses.exampleCN: 在中世纪，一道绝罚令使罪人不得参与一切圣事。
senses.why: This is the original technical sense: the Greek thing set up, later a devoted offering, then devoted to destruction.
senses.whyCN: 这是原本的专门含义：希腊语中「献置之物」先指献给神的祭品，后转为献给毁灭的诅咒之物。

intro.en: Anathema comes from Greek anatithenai, to set up as an offering, whose noun anathema later meant a thing cursed.
intro.cn: anathema 源于希腊语 anatithenai「献置」，其名词 anathema 后来转为「受诅咒之物」。

items.en: The root *dheh1- meant to set or to put, seen also in English do.
items.cn: 词根 *dheh1- 表示「放置、安置」，英语 do 也出自同一词根。

items.en: Anatithenai meant to set up or dedicate; the noun anathema first meant an offering set up in a temple.
items.cn: 希腊语 anatithenai 意为「献置、奉献」；名词 anathema 最初指供奉在神庙中的祭品。

items.en: In the Greek Bible, anathema translated a Hebrew term for something devoted to destruction, so it took on the sense of an accursed thing.
items.cn: 在希腊文《圣经》中，anathema 用来翻译希伯来语「当灭之物」，于是染上了「受诅咒」的强烈贬义。

items.en: Church Latin borrowed anathema as the formal term for excommunication and condemnation.
items.cn: 教会拉丁语借入 anathema，作为「绝罚、谴责」的正式术语。

items.en: English anathema appears in the 1520s in the churchly sense, and by the 17th century also named any detested thing or person.
items.cn: 英语 anathema 于 1520 年代以宗教义进入英语，到 17 世纪也用来指任何令人憎恶的人或事物。

note.en: Anathema looks like anthem but is unrelated; it sits near abhorrence and bane in meaning.
note.cn: anathema 拼写与 anthem 相近但词源无关；语义上与 abhorrence、bane 相近。

entries.definition: a solemn song of praise or loyalty
entries.definitionCN: 颂歌；国歌，只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自古英语 antefn

entries.definition: to curse or formally condemn
entries.definitionCN: 诅咒；革出教门，由 anathema 派生的动词

entries.definition: a lack of red blood cells
entries.definitionCN: 贫血，同为 an- 开头的希腊借词，但词根不同只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a library or cultural institution
entries.definitionCN: 图书馆；文艺学会，与雅典娜相关，与 anathema 无词源关系

entries.definition: a feeling of intense disgust
entries.definitionCN: 憎恶；深恶痛绝，强调情感本身

entries.definition: a cause of great distress or death
entries.definitionCN: 祸根；毒物，强调造成毁坏的原因

entries.definition: a solemn utterance calling for harm
entries.definitionCN: 诅咒，指诅咒的言语或行为，anathema 是其宗教化的正式形式

entries.definition: official exclusion from a church
entries.definitionCN: 绝罚；逐出教会，与 anathema 的宗教专门义对应

entries.definition: an outcast rejected by society
entries.definitionCN: 被社会排斥者，与「遭憎恶的人」义项相近

normalIntro.en: Split anathema into an- and thema to hold its Greek shape in mind.
normalIntro.cn: 把 anathema 拆成 an- 和 thema 来记住它的希腊语形状。

normal.en: ana- is a Greek prefix meaning up or back, as in analogy.
normal.cn: 前缀 ana- 表示「向上、回返」，如 analogy 中的用法。

normal.en: thema means something laid down or set up, the same root as theme.
normal.cn: thema 表示「被放置之物」，与 theme（主题）同根。

normal.en: Set up before the god first meant an offering, then a cursed thing.
normal.cn: 「献于神前」最初指祭品，后来转为受诅咒之物。

normal.en: The verb is anathematize, to pronounce the curse.
normal.cn: 动词 anathematize 意为「宣布诅咒、革出教门」。

normal.en: The common phrase is be anathema to someone.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 be anathema to someone「令某人深恶痛绝」。

abstract.en: Picture a figure pointed at by the whole village, unwelcome everywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被全村人指着的人，走到哪儿都不受欢迎。

abstract.en: See garlic held up to a vampire: the very thing he cannot bear.
abstract.cn: 想象大蒜举到吸血鬼面前：那是他最无法忍受之物。

abstract.en: Feel a word so heavy that saying it makes the room go silent.
abstract.cn: 感受一个词重得让整个房间瞬间安静下来的分量。

examples.en: Violence of any kind is anathema to her.
examples.cn: 任何形式的暴力都令她深恶痛绝。

examples.en: The council pronounced an anathema against the rebels.
examples.cn: 公会议对叛乱者宣布了绝罚。

examples.en: For a free-market economist, price controls are anathema.
examples.cn: 对自由市场经济学家来说，价格管制是不能容忍的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿那-thema」——阿婆那本书被当成诅咒之物，人人憎恶：anathema，令人憎恶的东西。

root: 希腊语 ana-（向上、回返）+ thema（被放置之物，词根 *dheh1-「放置」）→ anathema「献置之物」，经《圣经》希腊语转义为「当灭之物、受诅咒者」，再经教会拉丁语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from the formal church curse, to the cursed person, to anything detested.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从教会的正式诅咒出发，到被诅咒之人，再泛化为任何令人憎恶的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something set aside and cursed by everyone
core.cn: 核心意象：被众人搁置并诅咒的东西

branches.en: The original solemn church curse
branches.cn: 原本的教会正式诅咒

branches.en: The person the curse falls upon
branches.cn: 诅咒所加于其身的人

branches.en: Any detested thing or idea
branches.cn: 泛化的令人憎恶的事物或观念

branches.en: Being shunned by the whole group
branches.cn: 被整个群体避之唯恐不及

branches.en: From religious ban to everyday abhorrence
branches.cn: 从宗教禁令到日常憎恶的引申路径

intro.en: Anathema shows the Greek prefix ana- plus the root thema, to set up.
intro.cn: anathema 由希腊语前缀 ana- 加词根 thema「放置」构成。

latinIntro.en: The word passed through church Latin, and related forms keep the Greek shape.
latinIntro.cn: 该词经教会拉丁语传递，相关形式保留希腊语形状。

items.exampleCN: 主题（被设定下来的东西）
绰号（加于名上之词，同源词族）
综合（同根 them- 的放置义）
假设（放在底下作基础的，同根词）

definition_zh: 代谢；分解；把物质在体内转化（为能量或别的物质）
definition_en: to subject a substance to the chemical changes of metabolism, breaking it down or converting it into something else
core_image: 一台机器把一块原料吞进去，从另一头送出小零件与热量，机器本身毫发无损
scene: 这里指「代谢」。 The liver can metabolize only a limited amount of alcohol per hour.
sceneCN: 这里 metabolize 指「分解、转化某物」（第 1 个义项：对物质施加代谢性化学改造）；肝脏每小时只能处理有限量的酒精。图中可辨识物件：吞料的机器、原料块、送出的零件、散出的热。

pos.zh: 代谢；分解（及物动词，常用被动 be metabolized）

senses.title: To act on a substance chemically
senses.titleCN: 代谢：对物质施以化学改造
senses.definition: to subject a substance to the chemical changes of metabolism
senses.definitionCN: 使某物质经历代谢性的化学变化
senses.example: Bacteria metabolize the oil that spills into the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌会代谢泄漏到海里的石油。
senses.why: the verb turns the noun of change into an action: whatever is acted on is put through that change.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把表示变化的名词转为动作：被作用的东西就被送进那场变化。

senses.title: To break food down
senses.titleCN: 分解营养：把食物拆成小件
senses.definition: to break a nutrient down into smaller molecules the body can use
senses.definitionCN: 把营养素拆成身体可用的小分子
senses.example: Cells metabolize starch into glucose within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞在几分钟内把淀粉分解成葡萄糖。
senses.why: digestion is the most familiar case, so the verb is first heard as breaking food apart.
senses.whyCN: 消化是最熟悉的情形，因此这个动词最初听上去就是把食物拆开。

senses.title: To alter a drug or poison
senses.titleCN: 转化药物：把外来分子改造
senses.definition: to convert a drug or toxin into other compounds, usually in the liver
senses.definitionCN: 把药物或毒物转化为其他化合物，通常在肝脏中进行
senses.example: The enzyme metabolizes the drug into an inactive form.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酶把该药代谢成失活形式。
senses.why: the same action applied to foreign molecules is detoxification, and the verb carries that clinical sense.
senses.whyCN: 同样的作用施加于外来分子就是解毒，这个动词也带上了这层临床含义。

senses.title: To release energy from fuel
senses.titleCN: 转化为能量：从燃料取出可用能
senses.definition: to convert fuel into usable energy, as in cellular respiration
senses.definitionCN: 把燃料转化为可用能量，如细胞呼吸
senses.example: Muscle metabolizes fat during long, slow exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间慢速运动时肌肉代谢脂肪。
senses.why: because the change yields energy, the verb also names the extraction of power, not only the breakdown.
senses.whyCN: 由于变化会产出能量，这个动词也命名动力的提取，而不只是拆解。

senses.title: To be cleared away
senses.definition: to be removed from the body by metabolism, said of a substance in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 指某物质经代谢被从体内清除，多用被动语态
senses.example: Caffeine is metabolized within a few hours in most adults.
senses.exampleCN: 多数成年人几小时内就把咖啡因代谢掉。
senses.why: in the passive, the focus moves from the agent to the substance that disappears, so the verb means 'cleared'.
senses.whyCN: 在被动语态中，焦点从作用者移到消失的物质，因此这个动词意为「被清除」。

senses.title: How fast the body handles it
senses.definition: to handle a substance at a certain rate, as in 'metabolized quickly'
senses.definitionCN: 以一定速率处理某物，如「被迅速代谢」
senses.example: Some people metabolize caffeine much faster than others.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人代谢咖啡因比其他人快得多。
senses.why: rate adverbs attach naturally to the verb, so it also reports speed of handling.
senses.whyCN: 速率副词自然附着在这个动词上，因此它也报告处理的快慢。

senses.title: To digest an idea, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 比喻：消化吸收信息或想法
senses.definition: used figuratively for taking in and absorbing information or an experience
senses.definitionCN: 引申指把信息或经历吸纳、消化
senses.example: Give the team time to metabolize the new findings.
senses.exampleCN: 给团队一些时间去消化这些新发现。
senses.why: the body's handling of matter is borrowed for the mind's handling of ideas, a common figurative extension.
senses.whyCN: 身体处理物质的方式被借用于心智处理想法，这是常见的比喻延伸。

senses.title: To convert along a pathway
senses.definition: to convert one compound into another along a defined biochemical pathway
senses.definitionCN: 沿确定的生化途径把一种化合物转化为另一种
senses.example: The fungus metabolizes the sugar into an acid.
senses.exampleCN: 这种真菌把糖代谢成一种酸。
senses.why: in biochemistry the verb marks the direction of a conversion, from substrate to product.
senses.whyCN: 在生物化学中，这个动词标记转化的方向，从底物到产物。

intro.en: Metabolize is metabolism plus the verb suffix -ize, from Greek -izein through Latin and French. The base is Greek metabolē 'a change'.
intro.cn: metabolize 是 metabolism 加动词后缀 -ize，后者由希腊 -izein 经拉丁语与法语传入；词基是希腊 metabolē「变化」。

items.en: Greek -izein formed verbs meaning 'to make, to act in the manner of'. It passed into Latin as -izare and into French as -iser.
items.cn: 希腊 -izein 构成动词，意为「使……、以……方式行事」。它进入拉丁语为 -izare、法语为 -iser。

items.en: metabolē 'a change, a turning over' comes from meta- 'over' plus ballein 'to throw'; English metabolism first meant change in general.
items.cn: metabolē「变化、翻转」由 meta-「越过」加 ballein「投掷」构成；英语 metabolism 最初泛指变化。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the verb appears in nineteenth-century physiology after metabolism had been narrowed to the body's chemistry, and the exact first citation is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该动词在 metabolism 被收窄为体内化学之后出现于 19 世纪生理学；确切最早书证并无记录。

items.en: Twentieth-century pharmacology made 'metabolize a drug' a standard phrase, adding the sense of clearing foreign compounds.
items.cn: 20 世纪药理学使「代谢某药」成为标准说法，加入了清除外来化合物的义项。

items.en: Late twentieth-century writing extended the verb to ideas and experiences, as in 'metabolize new information'.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期的写作把该动词延伸到想法与经历，如「消化新信息」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): ballein has no agreed pre-Greek origin, so any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ballein 在希腊语之前的来源并无共识，其背后的印欧形式属重构，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: Group one holds the same-family words that differ in part of speech; group two holds ordinary verbs for the same handling seen without the technical frame.
note.cn: 第一组是同族但词性不同的词；第二组是不带技术框架、表达同样处理的普通动词。

entries.definition: The process itself, not an action on a substance. It cannot take an object.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身，不是对物质的作用；不能带宾语。

entries.definition: A substance made or used during metabolism. It is the result, while metabolize is the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指代谢中生成或消耗的物质；是结果，而 metabolize 是动作。

entries.definition: A person or organ that metabolizes, often classified as fast or slow; it names the doer, not the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行代谢的人或器官，常分为快慢型；命名行动者，不是行为。

entries.definition: To spread, as a tumour does, from meta- plus stasis 'standing'. It looks like metabolize but shares no ballein.
entries.definitionCN: 指像肿瘤那样转移，由 meta- 加 stasis「站立」构成；形似 metabolize，却并不共享 ballein。

entries.definition: To break food down in the gut; metabolism also happens inside cells and to drugs.
entries.definitionCN: 指在肠道中分解食物；代谢也发生在细胞内，也作用于药物。

entries.definition: A neutral phrase for splitting a substance apart; it lacks the biochemical frame of metabolize.
entries.definitionCN: 拆分物质的普通说法；没有 metabolize 的生物化学框架。

entries.definition: To change one thing into another; metabolize adds that the change is part of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指把一物变为另一物；metabolize 补充说明该变化属于代谢。

entries.definition: To handle something by a procedure; it can mean almost anything and is far broader than metabolize.
entries.definitionCN: 指按程序处理某物；含义极宽，远大于 metabolize。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: metabolism + -ize: to put a substance through metabolism.
normal.cn: metabolism + -ize：把某物送进代谢。

normal.en: The verb forms run metabolize, metabolizes, metabolized, metabolizing.
normal.cn: 动词形式为 metabolize、metabolizes、metabolized、metabolizing。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: metabolize glucose, metabolize a drug, rapidly metabolized, poorly metabolized.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：代谢葡萄糖、代谢药物、被迅速代谢、代谢不良。

normal.en: The passive is common in pharmacology: the drug is metabolized in the liver.
normal.cn: 药理学中常用被动：药物在肝脏被代谢。

normal.en: Metabolize takes an object; metabolism does not. That one fact keeps them apart.
normal.cn: metabolize 带宾语，metabolism 不带；这一条就能区分二者。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that swallows a block and sends out small parts and heat.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器吞进一块料，送出小零件与热。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen that turns one ingredient into three dishes.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房把一种原料做成三道菜。

abstract.en: Picture a reader who turns a dense page into something the mind can keep.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者把密密的文字变成心里留得住的东西。

examples.en: Some gut bacteria metabolize fibre into short fatty acids.
examples.cn: 一些肠道细菌把纤维代谢成短链脂肪酸。

examples.en: The patient metabolizes the anaesthetic slowly and needs a lower dose.
examples.cn: 该患者代谢麻醉药较慢，需要更低剂量。

examples.en: Yeast metabolizes sugar into alcohol when oxygen is scarce.
examples.cn: 缺氧时酵母把糖代谢成酒精。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「代谢（metabolism）＋ize」——让某物走一遍代谢流程 → 代谢、分解

root: 希腊 metabolē「变化」（meta- + ballein「投掷」）→ metabolism + 希腊 -izein（经拉丁 -izare、法语 -iser）→ metabolize。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one action: a machine swallows a substance and sends out parts and heat; that action is read as chemical handling, as breaking food, as altering drugs, as releasing energy, as being cleared, as a rate, as digesting ideas, and as a direction along a pathway.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一台机器吞下物质，送出零件与热；这一动作依次被读成化学处理、拆解食物、改造药物、释放能量、被清除、处理速率、消化想法，以及沿通路的方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a machine that swallows a block and sends out small parts and heat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台吞进料块、送出小零件与热的机器。

branches.en: THE ACTION: putting a substance through the chemical change.
branches.cn: 动作本身：使某物经历化学变化。

branches.en: FOOD: the familiar case of breaking a nutrient into usable pieces.
branches.cn: 食物：把营养素拆成可用小件的熟悉情形。

branches.en: FOREIGN MATTER: altering drugs and toxins, and being cleared from the body.
branches.cn: 外来物：改造药物与毒物，以及被从体内清除。

branches.en: POWER AND PACE: energy taken from fuel, and the rate at which it is handled.
branches.cn: 动力与节奏：从燃料取出能量，以及处理的快慢。

branches.en: MIND AND PATHWAY: ideas absorbed, and a conversion with a direction.
branches.cn: 心智与通路：想法被吸收，以及有方向的转化。

intro.en: Metabolize is a Greek-derived noun plus the Greek verb suffix -izein, which reached English through Latin -izare and French -iser.
intro.cn: metabolize 是希腊来源名词加希腊动词后缀 -izein，后者经拉丁 -izare 与法语 -iser 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies -izare, the borrowed form of Greek -izein, and New Latin metabolismus is a spelling rather than an inherited word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 -izare，即希腊 -izein 的借入形式；新拉丁语 metabolismus 只是拼写，不是传承词。

items.meaning: to put a substance through metabolism
items.example: The liver metabolizes the compound slowly.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏缓慢地代谢该化合物。

items.example: The drug is metabolized within hours.
items.exampleCN: 该药在数小时内被代谢。

items.example: The tissue is actively metabolizing fat.
items.exampleCN: 该组织正在活跃地代谢脂肪。

items.example: Only part of the sugar is metabolizable.

items.exampleCN: 快代谢者需要更高剂量。

latinEntries.meaning: to make, to act in the manner of

definition_zh: 贪得的；渴望获取的；占有欲强的；（犯罪）以获取财物为目的的
definition_en: strongly eager to acquire possessions, money or knowledge, sometimes to an excessive degree
core_image: 手不断伸向货架，车里越堆越满却仍不满足
scene: 商场大促，推着购物车的人一件接一件往里塞，轮子都快压弯了。 An acquisitive shopper rarely leaves a sale empty-handed.
sceneCN: 这里 acquisitive 是「渴望获取的」（第 1 个义项：强烈想要得到财物）；句意为一个贪得的购物者很少空手离开促销现场。

pos.zh: 形容词：贪得的；渴望获取的；占有欲强的

collocations.zh: 以获取财物为目的的犯罪

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「获得；取得」
由动词加 -ition 构成，义为「获得；收购」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「贪得；占有欲」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「贪求地；以获取的方式」

senses.title: Eager to acquire possessions
senses.definition: strongly wanting to obtain money, goods or property, often more than one needs
senses.definitionCN: 强烈想要得到金钱、物品或财产，往往超出实际需要
senses.example: The acquisitive heir bought three houses in a single year.
senses.exampleCN: 这位贪得的继承人一年之内买了三栋房子。
senses.why: Acquire means to obtain, and the -itive suffix marks a tendency, so the word describes a person pulled toward obtaining things.
senses.whyCN: acquire 意为「获得」，-itive 后缀标记一种倾向，所以这个词描述被「获取」牵着走的人。

senses.title: Materialistic, as a society
senses.definition: describing a culture or group that measures worth by what people own and buy
senses.definitionCN: 形容以人们拥有和购买的东西衡量价值的文化或群体
senses.example: Critics call the city acquisitive because every advertisement promises more.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这座城市物质至上，因为每则广告都在许诺更多。
senses.why: When the tendency spreads from one person to a whole culture, the word becomes a judgement about shared values.
senses.whyCN: 当这种倾向从一个人扩散到整个文化，这个词就变成对共同价值观的判断。

senses.title: Acquisitive crime
senses.titleCN: 以获取财物为目的的犯罪
senses.definition: in law, a crime committed mainly to obtain money or property, such as theft or fraud
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指主要为取得金钱或财产而实施的犯罪，如盗窃或诈骗
senses.example: The report separates acquisitive crime from violent crime.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把以获取财物为目的的犯罪与暴力犯罪区分开来。
senses.why: Law needs a label for motive rather than act, and acquisitive names the gain-seeking motive precisely.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要按动机而不是按行为分类的标签，acquisitive 恰好点明「为获取」的动机。

senses.title: An acquisitive instinct
senses.definition: in psychology, a natural drive to collect, hold and accumulate resources
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指收集、持有并积累资源的天然驱动力
senses.example: Some researchers treat the acquisitive instinct as a survival mechanism.
senses.exampleCN: 一些研究者把获取本能视为一种生存机制。
senses.why: If obtaining is a tendency, it can also be described as an inborn drive rather than a moral failing.
senses.whyCN: 如果获取是一种倾向，它也可以被描述为先天的驱动力，而不只是道德缺陷。

senses.title: Growth by buying other companies
senses.definition: in business, describing a strategy of growing by purchasing other firms rather than by internal expansion
senses.definitionCN: 商业中指靠收购其他公司而非内部扩张来增长的策略
senses.example: The acquisitive group added two rivals to its portfolio last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个靠收购扩张的集团上季度把两个竞争对手收入旗下。
senses.why: Companies acquire other companies, so the same word moves from personal greed to corporate strategy.
senses.whyCN: 公司收购其他公司，于是同一个词从个人贪欲转到了企业战略。

senses.title: Eager to acquire knowledge
senses.definition: strongly eager to learn, collect information or master new skills
senses.definitionCN: 强烈渴望学习、收集信息或掌握新技能
senses.example: Her acquisitive mind read every book on the reading list twice.
senses.exampleCN: 她那渴求知识的头脑把书单上的每本书读了两遍。
senses.why: The object of acquisition can be knowledge instead of goods, which turns a suspect trait into a praised one.
senses.whyCN: 获取的对象可以是知识而不是财物，这就把原本可疑的特质变成被称赞的品质。

senses.title: Hoarding behaviour in animals
senses.definition: in animal behaviour, the tendency to gather and store food beyond immediate need
senses.definitionCN: 动物行为学中指收集并储存超过当下所需食物的倾向
senses.example: The acquisitive squirrel filled every hollow in the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那只贪囤的松鼠把旧墙里的每个洞都塞满了。
senses.why: Hoarding is acquisition without immediate use, so the human word extends naturally to animal caching.
senses.whyCN: 囤积是获取而不立即使用，所以这个人类词汇自然延伸到动物的贮藏行为。

senses.title: Grasping attachment
senses.definition: in ethical and Buddhist contexts, the mental habit of grasping at things as if they could be permanently owned
senses.definitionCN: 在伦理与佛教语境中，指把事物当作可永久拥有而紧紧抓取的心理习惯
senses.example: Meditation aims to soften the acquisitive grip of the mind.
senses.exampleCN: 冥想旨在软化内心那种贪著不放的抓取。
senses.why: The word's image of a hand that will not let go becomes a moral and spiritual diagnosis of attachment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词「不肯松手」的画面，变成对执著的心理与精神诊断。

intro.en: Acquisitive comes from the Latin verb for seeking and obtaining, with a suffix that turns an action into a tendency.
intro.cn: acquisitive 来自拉丁语表示「寻求并获得」的动词，加上把动作变成倾向的后缀。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, ask or search for; it is also the source of question and inquiry.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻找、询问」，也是 question 与 inquiry 的来源。

items.en: Ad plus quaerere formed acquirere, to get in addition, to obtain; the past participle is acquisitus.
items.cn: ad 与 quaerere 构成 acquirere，意为「额外取得、获得」；其过去分词是 acquisitus。

items.en: Acquisitivus was used in medieval Latin for having the quality of acquiring.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 acquisitivus 表示「具有获取性质的」。

items.en: Old French acquerre carried the verb into English, while the adjective came later by a learned route.
items.cn: 古法语 acquerre 把动词带入英语，形容词则更晚经由学术路径进入。

items.en: The adjective acquisitive is recorded in English in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 acquisitive 在十六世纪见于英语记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word split into a moral sense, a legal sense and a business sense, all keeping the idea of obtaining.
items.cn: 这个词分化出道德义、法律义与商业义，但都保留「获取」的核心理念。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the acquire family; the near-meaning group gathers words for greed and desire with different intensity.
note.cn: 形近组收 acquire 词族；近义组收表达贪欲与渴望的词，强度各不相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to obtain or gain something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得、取得」，是本词的核心动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of obtaining something, or a company that has been bought.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「获得」或「被收购的公司」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being acquisitive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贪得、占有欲」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: Necessary or required; it looks close to acquisitive but comes from requirere, to require.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「必需的」，拼写接近 acquisitive，但词源是 requirere「要求」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Eager to ask questions and learn; it shares the quaerere root but aims at knowledge, not property.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「好奇好问的」，共享 quaerere 词根，但指向知识而非财产。

entries.definition: Wanting far more than one needs, especially food or money; harsher and more emotional than acquisitive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「贪婪的」，尤指食物或金钱，语气比 acquisitive 更重、更情绪化。

entries.definition: Valuing possessions and money above other things; a judgement about values, not a drive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「物质主义的」，是对价值观的判断，而不是描述驱动力。

entries.definition: Strongly desiring what belongs to someone else; formal and slightly old-fashioned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「觊觎的」，强烈想得到别人所有之物，语气正式且略旧。

entries.definition: Wanting to keep and control what one already has; it points inward to existing belongings.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「占有欲强的」，强调守住已拥有之物，方向向内。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real quaerere root and the legal and business phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 quaerere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的法律与商业搭配。

normal.en: Acquire is ad plus quaerere, to seek toward oneself; acquisitive is the habit of doing so.
normal.cn: acquire 是 ad 加 quaerere「朝自己寻求」，acquisitive 就是不断这样做的习惯。

normal.en: Inquisitive shares the same seeking root but seeks answers instead of things.
normal.cn: inquisitive 共享同一个「寻求」词根，但它寻求的是答案而不是东西。

normal.en: Acquisitive crime is a legal label for crimes committed for gain.
normal.cn: acquisitive crime 是法律标签，指为获利而实施的犯罪。

normal.en: An acquisitive company grows by buying other companies.
normal.cn: acquisitive 公司靠收购其他公司来扩张。

normal.en: The -itive ending, as in competitive, marks a tendency rather than a single act.
normal.cn: 与 competitive 相同的 -itive 结尾，标记的是一种倾向而非一次动作。

abstract.en: Picture a shopping cart that fills faster than it moves, because the hand keeps reaching.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆购物车装货比前进还快，因为那只手一直在伸。

abstract.en: The same hand can reach for books instead of goods, and then the word becomes praise.
abstract.cn: 同一只手也可以伸向书本而不是货物，这时这个词就变成赞美。

abstract.en: Acquisitive desire is a grip: the problem is not the object but the fingers that will not open.
abstract.cn: 贪求是一种抓握：问题不在物件，而在那几根不肯松开的手指。

examples.en: An acquisitive culture may confuse having more with being better.
examples.cn: 一个贪求的文化可能把「拥有更多」误当成「变得更好」。

examples.en: The court treated the theft as an acquisitive crime rather than a violent one.
examples.cn: 法院把这起盗窃视为以获取财物为目的的犯罪，而非暴力犯罪。

examples.en: Her acquisitive reading habits made her an expert in three fields.
examples.cn: 她渴求知识的阅读习惯使她成为三个领域的专家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿奎西提夫」——阿奎的手总往货架上伸，拿到手还要再拿：贪得的

root: 拉丁语 quaerere「寻找、询问」加 ad- 构成 acquirere「取得」，过去分词 acquisitus；中世纪拉丁语 acquisitivus 加 -itive「倾向」构成形容词。quaerere 也是 question 与 inquiry 的词源。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all follow one reaching hand: it takes possessions, shapes a whole culture, supplies a legal motive, becomes an instinct, buys companies, reaches for knowledge, hoards food, or will not let go in a spiritual sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都跟着同一只伸出的手：它抓财物、塑造整个文化、构成法律动机、变成本能、收购公司、伸向知识、囤积食物，或在精神层面不肯松手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand keeps reaching for more while the cart is already full.
core.cn: 核心意象：购物车已经装满，那只手仍在不断伸向更多。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the basic sense of wanting to obtain goods.
branches.cn: 个人线：想要获得财物的基本义。

branches.en: THE VALUE: the same drive becomes a judgement about society or a spiritual attachment.
branches.cn: 价值线：同一驱动力变成对社会价值的判断，或精神上的执著。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: law and business each give the drive an institutional name.
branches.cn: 制度线：法律与商业分别给这股驱动力一个制度化的名字。

branches.en: THE INSTINCT: psychology and animal behaviour describe it as inborn hoarding.
branches.cn: 本能线：心理学与动物行为学把它描述为先天的囤积倾向。

branches.en: THE MIND: when the object is knowledge, the tendency turns into a virtue.
branches.cn: 心智线：当对象是知识时，这种倾向就转为美德。

intro.en: Acquisitive joins a Latin prefix, a Latin seeking root and an adjective suffix that marks tendency.
intro.cn: acquisitive 由拉丁语前缀、表示「寻求」的拉丁词根，以及标记倾向的形容词后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere, acquirere and acquisitus are recorded; the adjective acquisitivus is medieval.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quaerere、acquirere、acquisitus 均有记录；形容词 acquisitivus 属中世纪拉丁语。

It is the seeking root of the family.

items.example: It joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: 它把前缀与词根结合起来。
它构成 inquisitive，指向寻求答案。

definition_zh: 引力；万有引力；被吸引而趋近的作用或趋势
definition_en: the force by which bodies attract one another, or the tendency to move toward something
core_image: 两只铁球之间那根看不见的绳把彼此慢慢拉近，桌上散落的碎屑也跟着滚向它们
scene: 把苹果落地说成万物互相吸引，你说 Gravitation holds the planets in their orbits.
sceneCN: 这里 gravitation 指「物体之间相互吸引的作用」（第 2 个义项：支配天体运动的万有引力）；句意为引力使行星保持在轨道上。图中可辨识物件：行星轨道、中心恒星、看不见的拉力线、苹果。

pos.zh: 引力；万有引力；吸引趋势（不可数）

derivatives.zh: gravity + -on（粒子后缀）：引力子（理论假设粒子）

senses.title: The attraction between bodies
senses.titleCN: 物体之间相互吸引的作用
senses.definition: the force by which any two bodies with mass attract each other
senses.definitionCN: 任何两个有质量的物体相互吸引的作用力
senses.example: Gravitation pulls the two spheres together.
senses.exampleCN: 引力把两个球体拉近。
senses.why: the noun comes from Latin gravitas 'weight', because the most familiar sign of this attraction is that things have weight.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自拉丁 gravitas「重量」，因为这种吸引最常见的表现就是物体有重量。

senses.title: Universal gravitation
senses.titleCN: 万有引力：支配天体运动的普遍规律
senses.definition: the principle that every mass attracts every other mass, which governs orbits
senses.definitionCN: 每个质量都吸引其他质量、并支配轨道的原理
senses.example: Gravitation holds the planets in their orbits.
senses.exampleCN: 引力使行星保持在轨道上。
senses.why: universal marks the leap from falling apples to moving planets: the same rule was found to work at both scales.
senses.whyCN: universal 标出从落下的苹果到运行的行星这一跃迁：同一条规则被发现在两个尺度上都成立。

senses.title: Curved spacetime
senses.titleCN: 广义相对论中的时空弯曲
senses.definition: the modern description in which gravitation is the curvature of spacetime rather than a pull
senses.definitionCN: 现代描述：引力是时空的弯曲，而非一种拉力
senses.example: In general relativity, gravitation is geometry.
senses.exampleCN: 在广义相对论中，引力就是几何。
senses.why: the modern sense replaces the pull with a shape: bodies follow the straightest path through curved spacetime.
senses.whyCN: 现代义用形状取代拉力：天体在弯曲时空中走最直的路径。

senses.title: The act of being drawn down
senses.definition: the process of moving toward a mass under its attraction
senses.definitionCN: 在吸引作用下朝某个质量运动的过程
senses.example: The gravitation of the cloud collapsed it into a disk.
senses.exampleCN: 云气的引力坍缩把它压成一个盘。
senses.why: the noun can name the process as well as the force, which is why astronomers speak of gravitation acting on a cloud.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既可指力，也可指过程，因此天文学家会说引力作用于云气。

senses.title: Mutual attraction between people
senses.titleCN: 人与人之间的相互吸引
senses.definition: a figurative use for the mutual draw between people
senses.definitionCN: 比喻人与人之间相互吸引
senses.example: There was a strange gravitation between the two strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 两个陌生人之间有一种奇怪的吸引。
senses.why: the physical pull becomes social: two people move toward each other without any visible force.
senses.whyCN: 物理的拉力转为社交义：两个人没有任何可见的力也彼此靠近。

senses.title: A drift of opinion
senses.definition: a tendency of opinion or activity to move toward a particular point
senses.definitionCN: 意见或活动朝某一特定方向移动的倾向
senses.example: The gravitation of voters toward the centre changed the race.
senses.exampleCN: 选民向中间靠拢的趋势改变了选情。
senses.why: once a group is imagined as masses, its drift is described with the same word as a falling body.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把群体想象成许多质量，它的漂移就用与落体相同的词来描述。

senses.title: Gravitational collapse
senses.definition: the process by which gravity causes a cloud or a star to collapse and bind matter
senses.definitionCN: 引力使云气或恒星坍缩并把物质束缚起来的过程
senses.example: Gravitation overcame the pressure and the core collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 引力压过了压力，核心坍缩了。
senses.why: collapse is gravitation winning: the inward pull exceeds every outward push, and the object shrinks.
senses.whyCN: 坍缩就是引力获胜：向内的拉力超过一切向外的推力，天体于是缩小。

senses.title: The older sense of weighing
senses.definition: an older physical use for the act of weighing or the state of having weight
senses.definitionCN: 旧物理用法：称重的动作或有重量的状态
senses.example: Early texts used gravitation for the act of weighing a body.
senses.exampleCN: 早期文献用 gravitation 指称量物体的动作。
senses.why: the oldest sense is literal: gravitas is weight, so gravitation first named the business of weighing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是字面的：gravitas 就是重量，因此 gravitation 最初指称重这件事。

intro.en: Gravitation comes from Latin gravitas 'weight, heaviness', from gravis 'heavy', with the noun suffix -ation. Newton made it the name of a universal force in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gravitation 出自拉丁 gravitas「重量、沉重」，源于 gravis「重的」，加名词后缀 -ation。牛顿在 17 世纪使它成为普遍力的名称。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gravis meant 'heavy, weighty, serious', and also 'burdensome'; its deeper Indo-European origin is a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: gravis 意为「重的、有分量的、严肃的」，也指「令人负担的」；其更深的印欧来源属重构，而非有书证的形式。

items.en: Gravitas 'weight, heaviness, seriousness' supplied English gravity and gave the stem for gravitation.
items.cn: gravitas「重量、沉重、严肃」提供英语 gravity，并给出 gravitation 的词干。

items.en: The noun is recorded before Newton, but his Principia of 1687 set out universal gravitation and made gravitation the standard English name for the force acting between all masses.
items.cn: 这个名词在牛顿之前已有记录，但他 1687 年的《原理》阐述了万有引力，并使 gravitation 成为英语中指所有质量间作用力的标准名称。

items.en: After 1915 general relativity reinterpreted gravitation as the curvature of spacetime, and the older noun was kept for the same set of phenomena.
items.cn: 1915 年广义相对论把引力重新解释为时空弯曲，旧名词仍用于同一组现象。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was applied to social and psychological attraction, where bodies are replaced by people and opinions.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，这个词被用于社会与心理层面的吸引，其中的物体被换成人与意见。

items.en: Root uncertainty: the Indo-European shape behind gravis is a reconstruction. First-date uncertainty only: the earliest English use of gravitation in the physical sense is not precisely dated, and the seventeenth-century attribution follows Newton's publication rather than a printed first use.
items.cn: 词根存疑：gravis 背后的印欧形态属重构。仅首见年代存疑：gravitation 物理义最早的英语用例没有确切年代，17 世纪之说依据的是牛顿的出版而非某个最早印刷用例。

note.en: Group one holds the words of the same weight stock that are routinely confused; group two holds the neighbouring terms for the force and its effects.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「重」词干、常被混淆的词；第二组是邻近的力与效应术语。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for the force, and also for seriousness; gravitation is the formal term for the universal relation between masses.
entries.definitionCN: 日常指这种力的名词，也指严肃；gravitation 是质量之间普遍关系的正式术语。

entries.definition: The adjective formed from gravitation, as in gravitational waves; it cannot stand alone as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 由 gravitation 构成的形容词，如引力波；不能单独作名词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to move toward something by attraction, used mostly of people and preferences.
entries.definitionCN: 指受吸引而趋向某物的动词，多用于人与偏好。

entries.definition: Any force or tendency that draws things together, including magnetism and liking; gravitation is the specific mass-to-mass case.
entries.definitionCN: 任何使事物靠近的力或倾向，包括磁力与好感；gravitation 专指质量之间的情形。

entries.definition: The explicit phrase naming the force; gravitation can name the phenomenon or the theory, so the two overlap but are not identical.
entries.definitionCN: 明确指该力的短语；gravitation 可指现象或理论，两者重叠但不完全相同。

entries.definition: The force a body feels in a particular gravitational field; it is a measurement, not the universal relation.
entries.definitionCN: 物体在特定引力场中受到的力；它是一种测量值，不是那条普遍关系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin gravis 'heavy' + -ation: the business of heaviness.
normal.cn: 拉丁 gravis「重」+ -ation：关于「重」的事。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: universal gravitation, Newton's law of gravitation.
normal.cn: 固定短语：万有引力、牛顿引力定律。

normal.en: The family runs gravity, gravitational, gravitate, graviton.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gravity、gravitational、gravitate、graviton。

normal.en: Every mass attracts every other mass.
normal.cn: 每个质量都吸引其他质量。

normal.en: General relativity turns the pull into curvature.
normal.cn: 广义相对论把拉力变成弯曲。

abstract.en: Picture crumbs on a table all drifting toward one heavy bowl.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的碎屑都朝一个沉重的碗漂去。

abstract.en: Picture two strangers crossing a room without deciding to.
abstract.cn: 想象两个陌生人没打定主意却相互走近。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd slowly leaning toward one side of a square.
abstract.cn: 想象人群慢慢朝广场的一侧倾靠。

examples.en: Universal gravitation explains both the fall of an apple and the orbit of the moon.
examples.cn: 万有引力既能解释苹果落地，也能解释月球的轨道。

examples.en: Gravitation caused the gas cloud to collapse into a disk.
examples.cn: 引力使气体云坍缩成一个盘。

examples.en: Under general relativity, gravitation is described as curved spacetime.
examples.cn: 在广义相对论下，引力被描述为弯曲的时空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gravity（重力）+ ation」——重的东西彼此拉近 → 引力

root: 拉丁 gravitas「重量」← gravis「重的」+ -ation；牛顿 1687 年《原理》确立万有引力之名；gravis 的印欧来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pull: masses attract, the rule becomes universal, spacetime curves, matter falls and collapses, people and opinions drift, and an older sense still remembers that the word first meant weighing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种拉力展开：质量相互吸引；规则变得普遍、时空弯曲、物质下落与坍缩、人与意见漂移，最后一个旧义仍记得这个词最初指称重。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible cord between two heavy balls, drawing crumbs along the table toward them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个重球之间一根看不见的绳，把桌上的碎屑也拉向它们。

branches.en: THE PLAIN FORCE: masses attract one another.
branches.cn: 朴素的力：质量相互吸引。

branches.en: FROM LAW TO GEOMETRY: the universal rule, then curvature.
branches.cn: 从定律到几何：普遍规律，再到时空弯曲。

branches.en: MOVEMENT AND COLLAPSE: falling toward a mass, and the inward win that shrinks a cloud.
branches.cn: 运动与坍缩：朝质量下落，以及使云气缩小的向内胜利。

branches.en: DRAWN WITHOUT A FORCE: people and opinions drift together.
branches.cn: 没有力也被吸引：人与意见一起漂移。

branches.en: THE OLD WEIGHING: the word once named the act of weighing.
branches.cn: 旧日的称重：这个词曾指称重的动作。

intro.en: Gravitation is a Latin adjective stem plus a noun suffix; the same gravis family supplies gravity and gravitate, and the suffix -ation is highly productive.
intro.cn: gravitation 是拉丁形容词词干加名词后缀；同一 gravis 词族给出 gravity 与 gravitate，后缀 -ation 构词力很强。

latinIntro.en: Latin gravis and gravitas give gravity, gravitation and gravitate; the particle name graviton adds a Greek-style -on suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gravis 与 gravitas 给出 gravity、gravitation、gravitate；粒子名 graviton 加的是希腊式的 -on 后缀。

items.example: The root also gives grave in the sense of serious.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也给出 grave「严肃的」一义。

items.example: The noun supplies the stem of gravitation.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供 gravitation 的词干。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into the name of a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变为过程之名。

items.meaning: the process of being heavy or drawn
items.example: English built the noun on the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 英语在拉丁词干上构成这个名词。

items.example: The shorter noun keeps the everyday sense.
items.exampleCN: 较短的名词保留日常义。

items.example: The adjective is formed in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在英语中构成。

items.example: The verb is mostly figurative today.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词如今多用于比喻。

items.example: The suffix is modelled on electron and photon.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀模仿 electron 与 photon。

items.example: The prefix and root reverse the pull.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根反转了拉力。

definition_zh: 受让人；被指派人；承担人
definition_en: a person to whom a right, property, or task is legally assigned or transferred
core_image: 合同末尾签字栏里接过权利的那个人
scene: 律师把一份写满条款的合同推过桌面，指着最下面等待签名的一栏。 The assignee signed the contract and received all the rights to the patent.
sceneCN: 这里 assignee 是「受让人」（第 1 个义项：依法接受权利转让的人）；句意为受让人签署合同，取得了这项专利的全部权利。

pos.zh: 受让人（接受权利、财产转让者）
被指派承担任务的人

derivatives.zh: 动词本源，义为「指派；转让」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「转让；任务」
同族对偶词，义为「转让人」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「转让（旧义）；幽会」

senses.title: A person who receives rights by legal transfer
senses.definition: a party to whom property, rights, or interests are formally transferred
senses.definitionCN: 财产、权利或利益被正式转让给的当事方
senses.example: The assignee of the lease must honor its terms.
senses.exampleCN: 租约的受让人必须遵守其条款。
senses.why: The suffix -ee marks the person who receives the action, so the assignee is the one the assignment lands on.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ee 标记动作的承受者，受让人正是「转让」落在身上的那一方。

senses.title: A person to whom a task is assigned
senses.definition: a person designated to carry out a particular duty or job
senses.definitionCN: 被指定执行某项职责或工作的人
senses.example: Each assignee reported progress to the project manager.
senses.exampleCN: 每位被指派人都向项目经理汇报进展。
senses.why: Assignment spreads from law into ordinary work, and -ee keeps marking the receiver of the task.
senses.whyCN: assignment 从法律语境扩展到日常工作，-ee 依旧标记任务的承受者。

intro.en: Assignee comes from the verb assign with the legal suffix -ee, tracing back through Old French to Latin assignare.
intro.cn: assignee 由动词 assign 加法律后缀 -ee 构成，经古法语追溯至拉丁语 assignare。

items.en: Assignare meant to mark out, allot, from ad- plus signare, to mark.
items.cn: 拉丁语 assignare 意为标出、分配，出自 ad- 加 signare（作记号）。

items.en: Old French assigner carried the same sense of allotting.
items.cn: 古法语 assigner 保留了分配、指定之义。

items.en: Medieval legal French paired assign with the suffix -ee for the receiving party.
items.cn: 中世纪法律法语将 assign 与后缀 -ee 搭配，指接受一方。

items.en: English adopted assignee in legal use by the fifteenth to sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪英语在法律语境中采用 assignee。

items.en: It now covers both legal transfers and ordinary task assignments.
items.cn: 如今它既指法律转让的受让方，也指被分派任务的人。

note.en: The -ee suffix flips the roles: one signs away, the other signs on.
note.cn: 后缀 -ee 翻转了角色：一方让出，一方接手。

entries.definition: the party who transfers the rights
entries.definitionCN: 转让人（与受让人相对）

entries.definition: to transfer or appoint
entries.definitionCN: 转让；指派（动词本源）

entries.definition: person receiving rights outside formal records
entries.definitionCN: 事实受让人（短语形式）

entries.definition: electronic signing, unrelated root beyond sign
entries.definitionCN: 电子签名（拼写相近，实为 sign 的电子用法）

entries.definition: an appointment or a secret meeting
entries.definitionCN: 幽会；指定（同根旧义名词）

entries.definition: person to whom property is transferred
entries.definitionCN: 受转让人（近义法律用语）

entries.definition: person granted rights or property
entries.definitionCN: 被授予人

entries.definition: one who benefits from an arrangement
entries.definitionCN: 受益人

entries.definition: one who takes over a position or rights
entries.definitionCN: 继承人；继任者

entries.definition: person named to hold or receive something
entries.definitionCN: 被提名者；代名人

normalIntro.en: Break it as assign + ee: the ee is the one who ends up holding the rights.
normalIntro.cn: 拆成 assign + -ee：带 -ee 的那个就是最终接过权利的人。

normal.en: -ee marks the receiver, as in employee and trainee.
normal.cn: -ee 标记接受方，如 employee、trainee。

normal.en: assignor transfers, assignee receives.
normal.cn: assignor 转让，assignee 接受。

normal.en: in law the word belongs to contract language.
normal.cn: 在法律中它是合同术语。

normal.en: plural is assignees, spelled with a double e ending.
normal.cn: 复数为 assignees，以双 e 结尾。

normal.en: assignment names the act or document of transfer.
normal.cn: assignment 指转让行为或文书。

abstract.en: Picture a baton passed in a relay; the catcher is the assignee.
abstract.cn: 想象接力中递出的接力棒：接住它的就是受让人。

abstract.en: See two signature lines; the second name is the assignee.
abstract.cn: 看到两行签名栏：第二个名字是受让人。

abstract.en: Feel a package delivered; whoever signs for it is the assignee.
abstract.cn: 体会一件包裹送达：签收的人即受让人。

examples.en: The assignee recorded the transfer at the registry.
examples.cn: 受让人在登记处办理了转让登记。

examples.en: Each assignee received a clear list of duties.
examples.cn: 每位被指派人都拿到一份明确的职责清单。

examples.en: Courts protect the assignee against hidden defects in the claim.
examples.cn: 法院保护受让人免受权利中的隐性瑕疵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额赛你」——任务「额」来「赛」给「你」，你就是被指派、受让的人。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ signare（作记号）→ assignare（标出、分配）→ 古法语 assigner → 英语 assign 加法律后缀 -ee（承受者）。

sensesIntro.en: From signed transfers of rights come both legal assignees and everyday task holders.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「签字转让」长出法律上的受让人与日常的被指派人两支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name written on the receiving line of a contract
core.cn: 核心意象：合同受让栏上写下的名字

branches.en: receiving rights through legal transfer
branches.cn: 经法律转让接受权利

branches.en: being designated for a task
branches.cn: 被指定承担任务

branches.en: the receiving role marked by -ee
branches.cn: -ee 标记的承受角色

branches.en: entitlement recorded in documents
branches.cn: 文件记载的权利归属

branches.en: responsibility accepted in work settings
branches.cn: 工作场景中接下的职责

intro.en: Assignee shows how a legal suffix turns a verb into the receiving party.
intro.cn: assignee 展示了法律后缀如何把动词变成承受方名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin signare, to mark, is the seed of the whole assign family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 signare（作记号）是整个 assign 词族的种子。

definition_zh: n. 死亡；（制度、企业等的）终止，消亡；（不动产）转让 v. 遗赠；转让
definition_en: the death of a person or the end of something that used to exist
core_image: 老戏院的海报被雨泡烂，门锁换了新的，招牌上的字只剩一半
scene: 那场危机导致了公司的消亡。 The crisis led to the demise of the firm.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：demise 指终止、消亡；句意是那场危机导致了公司的消亡。

pos.zh: 死亡；终止；消亡；（不动产）转让
遗赠；转让（不动产）

senses.title: Death
senses.definition: the death of a person, used formally or euphemistically
senses.definitionCN: 人的死亡，正式或委婉的说法
senses.example: The family gathered after his demise.
senses.exampleCN: 他去世后家人聚到了一起。
senses.why: A black-bordered notice in a newspaper.
senses.whyCN: 报纸上一则黑框讣告。

senses.title: End of something
senses.definition: the end or failure of an institution, company or practice
senses.definitionCN: 机构、公司或做法的终结或失败
senses.example: The crisis led to the demise of the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 那场危机导致了公司的消亡。
senses.why: A theatre poster soaked through by rain.
senses.whyCN: 一张被雨泡烂的戏院海报。

senses.title: Transfer of property
senses.definition: the transfer of an estate by will or lease, in law
senses.definitionCN: 法律上以遗嘱或租约转让不动产
senses.example: The lease records the demise of the land.
senses.exampleCN: 租约记录了这块土地的转让。
senses.why: A deed handed across a desk with a seal.
senses.whyCN: 一份盖着印、递过桌面的契据。

intro.en: Demise comes from Latin demittere, de- plus mittere, to send: to hand something down or over.
intro.cn: demise 源自拉丁语 demittere，由 de- 加 mittere（送）构成：把东西交下去、交出去。

items.en: Mittere meant to send.
items.cn: mittere 意为送。

items.en: Demittere meant to send down or let go.
items.cn: demittere 意为放下、送走。

items.en: Demise entered English for transferring an estate.
items.cn: 十五世纪 demise 以转让不动产义进入英语。

items.en: The demise of the crown named the passing of sovereignty.
items.cn: demise of the crown 指王权的移交。

items.en: It softened into a formal word for death.
items.cn: 十八世纪委婉化为死亡的正式说法。

items.en: It now commonly names the end of a firm or practice.
items.cn: 如今常指公司或做法的终结。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the mis- sending family; the near-meaning group names other kinds of ending.
note.cn: 形近组共享 mis-（送）家族；近义组是其他「结束」的说法。

entries.definition: To send someone away or end a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 解散；驳回。

entries.definition: A statement that one will do something.
entries.definitionCN: 承诺。

entries.definition: To suppose something without evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 推测。

entries.definition: The end of a life.
entries.definitionCN: 死亡。

entries.definition: A sudden failure or falling down.
entries.definitionCN: 崩溃；倒塌。

entries.definition: The state of no longer existing.
entries.definitionCN: 灭绝。

normalIntro.en: Demise is de- plus mis- send: something is handed over and is no longer yours.
normalIntro.cn: demise 就是 de- 加 mis-（送）：东西被交出去了，不再属于你。

normal.en: Mis- means to send, as in mission.
normal.cn: mis- 意为送，如 mission。

normal.en: De- means down or away.
normal.cn: de- 表示向下、离开。

normal.en: In law, demise hands an estate over.
normal.cn: 法律上 demise 把不动产交出去。

normal.en: The demise of the crown passes the throne.
normal.cn: demise of the crown 指王位移交。

normal.en: A firm meets its demise when it closes.
normal.cn: 公司关门就是它的 demise。

examples.en: Two demises were recorded in the parish that year.

examples.en: The land was demised to his eldest son.

sensesIntro.en: One thing handed on: a life, a firm and a deed.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次交出去：一条命、一家公司与一份契据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soaked theatre poster, a new lock on the door and half a sign left

branches.en: A black-bordered notice in a newspaper.
branches.cn: 报纸上一则黑框讣告。

branches.cn: 一张被雨泡烂的戏院海报。

branches.en: A deed handed across a desk with a seal.

branches.en: Both mark something that will not continue.
branches.cn: 两者都标记某样东西不会再继续。

branches.en: Both pass what one held to another.
branches.cn: 两者都把一个人持有的东西交给另一方。

intro.en: Demise is de- plus mis-; the sending root builds the mission and dismissal family.

senses.title: Repairing a damaged thing

senses.definitionCN: 修复建筑、绘画或器物，使其回到较早状态的工作
senses.example: The restoration of the ceiling took seven years and three teams.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板的修复花了七年、换了三支队伍。
senses.why: Restoration aims at a former state, not a new one; the standard is the building as it once was, reconstructed from evidence.
senses.whyCN: 修复瞄准的是旧状态而非新状态；标准是建筑曾经的样子，并依据证据把它重新造出。

senses.title: Bringing order back
senses.titleCN: 恢复：让秩序与制度回到原状
senses.definition: the act of bringing a system, peace, or lawful order back into effect
senses.definitionCN: 使制度、和平或合法秩序重新生效的行为
senses.example: The new government promised the restoration of public services.
senses.exampleCN: 新政府承诺恢复公共服务。
senses.why: What is restored here is not matter but arrangement; the pieces still exist, and the task is to reattach them.
senses.whyCN: 这里修复的不是物质而是秩序；各个部件仍在，任务是把它们重新接上。

senses.title: Giving back what was taken
senses.titleCN: 归还：把拿走之物送回原主
senses.definition: the return of property, rights, or territory to the person or group that owned it
senses.definitionCN: 把财产、权利或领土归还给原先拥有的人或群体
senses.example: The treaty provided for the restoration of the seized archives.
senses.exampleCN: 条约规定归还被查扣的档案。
senses.why: The Latin verb could mean to give back; restoration is the undoing of a taking rather than the mending of a break.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词也有“归还”义；此义是撤销一次夺取，而不是修补一次破损。

senses.title: A dynasty back on the throne
senses.titleCN: 复辟：旧王朝或旧政权重新掌权
senses.definition: the return of a monarchy or former regime to power
senses.definitionCN: 君主制或旧政权重新掌权
senses.example: The Restoration of 1660 brought Charles II back to London.
senses.exampleCN: 一六六〇年的王政复辟使查理二世重返伦敦。
senses.why: A political order is treated as a thing that can be put back; the word lends the past a shape that can be reinstalled.
senses.whyCN: 政治秩序被当成一件可以放回原处的东西；这个词把过去赋予一种可以重新安装的形状。

senses.title: Strength coming back
senses.titleCN: 康复：体力与健康的恢复
senses.definition: the recovery of health, strength, or normal function after illness or exhaustion
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或耗竭之后健康、体力或正常功能的恢复
senses.example: Rest and good food brought about a slow restoration of his strength.
senses.exampleCN: 休息与良好的饮食使他的体力慢慢恢复。
senses.why: A body out of order is pictured as a damaged object, and its recovery as repair to the original working condition.
senses.whyCN: 失调的身体被想象成受损的器物，康复则被想象为修回原来的运转状态。

senses.title: Healing a landscape
senses.titleCN: 生态修复：让退化的生态系统恢复功能
senses.definition: the practice of helping a degraded ecosystem recover its structure, species, and functions
senses.definitionCN: 帮助退化的生态系统恢复结构、物种与功能的实践
senses.example: The wetland restoration reconnected the river to its floodplain.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地修复把河流重新接到它的泛滥平原。
senses.why: Ecologists borrow the word because a damaged marsh is treated as a broken system whose original functions can be rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家借用这个词，因为受损的沼泽被当作一个坏掉的系统，其原有功能可以被重建。

senses.title: The restored version
senses.titleCN: 修复版本：修复工作产出的成品
senses.definition: a version of a film, recording, or text produced by repair and cleaning
senses.definitionCN: 经修复与清理后产出的影片、录音或文本版本
senses.example: The restoration adds twelve minutes cut from the original release.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修复版本多出十二分钟原发行时被剪掉的片段。
senses.why: Here the noun names the product rather than the process; the work becomes a thing that can be screened or sold.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词命名的是成品而非过程；修复工作变成了一件可以放映或出售的东西。

senses.title: Recovering lost data
senses.titleCN: 恢复：从损坏介质中取回数据
senses.definition: the retrieval of data or files from damaged or deleted storage
senses.definitionCN: 从损坏或被删除的存储中取回数据或文件
senses.example: The restoration recovered most photographs from the failed drive.
senses.exampleCN: 这次数据恢复从故障硬盘中取回了大部分照片。
senses.why: Digital recovery repeats the old pattern: something lost is brought back into use by patient reconstruction.
senses.whyCN: 数字恢复重复了旧的模式：失去之物通过耐心重建被带回可用状态。

intro.en: Restoration is restore plus -ation. Restore comes from Latin restaurare, to renew or rebuild, whose second element is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: restoration 由 restore 加 -ation 构成。restore 出自拉丁语 restaurare“更新、重建”，其第二个成分的来源并不确定。

items.en: Restaurare meant to rebuild, repair, or renew. It is recorded in Roman use for restoring buildings and institutions.
items.cn: restaurare 意为重建、修理、更新。罗马文献用它指修复建筑与制度。

items.en: The element after re- is generally thought to come from a root meaning to stand, but its exact formation is uncertain.
items.cn: re- 之后的成分一般被认为来自表示“站立”的词根，但其确切构词来源不确定。

items.en: Instaurare, to set up or establish, shares this element, which supports the reading of a standing structure put back in place.
items.cn: instaurare“设立、建立”共享这一成分，支持“把立着的结构放回原处”这一理解。

items.en: Old French restaurer carried the architectural and medical senses into English: rebuilding a fabric and rebuilding a body.
items.cn: 古法语 restaurer 把建筑与医学两义带入英语：重建建筑物，也重建身体。

items.en: English restore took on the added sense of giving back property, which the Latin verb only occasionally carried.
items.cn: 英语 restore 增加了“归还财产”义，而拉丁动词只是偶尔带有此义。

items.en: The Latin suffix -ationem names an action or its result, so restoration can name either the work or the finished version.
items.cn: 拉丁后缀 -ationem 命名动作或其结果，因此 restoration 既可指工作，也可指修成的版本。

note.en: The first group is the restore family, separated by word class; the second compares words for repair, renewal, and recovery.
note.cn: 第一组是 restore 词族，按词类区分；第二组比较表示修理、更新与恢复的词。

entries.definition: to repair, bring back, or return something. It names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 修复、使恢复或归还；命名的是动作。

entries.definition: having the power to restore health or strength.
entries.definitionCN: 有恢复健康或体力作用的。

entries.definition: a person who repairs buildings, paintings, or furniture.
entries.definitionCN: 修复建筑、绘画或家具的人。

entries.definition: the work of making a building new again, often with modern changes. It permits improvement.
entries.definitionCN: 使建筑重新变新，常含现代化改造；允许改良。

entries.definition: the rebuilding of something destroyed, often from evidence or fragments.
entries.definitionCN: 重建被毁之物，常依据证据或残片。

entries.definition: the return to a normal state after loss, illness, or failure. It stresses the process of getting well.
entries.definitionCN: 在失去、患病或失败后回到正常状态；强调好转过程。

entries.definition: the mending of something broken so that it works again. It stresses function over historical accuracy.
entries.definitionCN: 修补破损之物使其重新可用；强调功能，而非历史准确性。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: restore plus -ation. The second element of the Latin verb is uncertain, so no invented root is offered.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：restore 加 -ation。该拉丁动词的第二个成分来源不确定，因此不编造词根。

normal.en: Restore plus ation: the work of putting something back as it was.
normal.cn: restore 加 ation：把某物放回原样的工作。

normal.en: A restored window lets in light the way it did a century ago.
normal.cn: 修好的窗户，让光像一百年前那样透进来。

normal.en: Restoring order is reattaching pieces that still exist.
normal.cn: 恢复秩序，就是把仍在的部件重新接上。

normal.en: Restoring archives is giving back, not mending.
normal.cn: 归还档案是物归原主，不是修补。

normal.en: Wetland restoration treats a marsh like a broken machine.
normal.cn: 湿地修复把沼泽当成一台坏掉的机器。

abstract.en: Every restoration is also an interpretation: someone decides which past state counts as the real one.
abstract.cn: 每次修复同时也是一次解释：总有人决定哪个过去才算“真正的原貌”。

abstract.en: To restore is to admit that the present version is not acceptable.
abstract.cn: 要修复，就得承认眼前的版本不可接受。

abstract.en: Restored objects carry two dates at once: the year they were made and the year they were saved.
abstract.cn: 被修复的物件同时带着两个年份：制成之年与获救之年。

examples.en: The restoration of the mosaic revealed colours that had been hidden under soot for centuries.
examples.cn: 马赛克镶嵌画的修复显露出被烟灰掩埋数百年的色彩。

examples.en: After the flood, the restoration of the railway took two years.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，铁路的修复花了两年。

examples.en: The film's restoration was based on three surviving prints.
examples.cn: 这部影片的修复依据三份幸存的拷贝。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（重新）+ store（储存、存放）——把旧样子重新存回去，就是修复。

root: 由 restore（修复、恢复、归还）加 -ation（名词后缀）构成；restore 出自拉丁语 restaurare“重建、更新”，该词第二个成分来源不确定，本义为“使某物回到原有状态的行为或成果”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of restoration, all circling one idea: an earlier condition is brought back. What returns may be a building, an order, a piece of property, a dynasty, a body's strength, an ecosystem, a cleaned film, or lost data.
sensesIntro.cn: restoration 的八个义项都围绕一个观念：让较早的状态回来。回来的可以是建筑、秩序、财产、王朝、体力、生态系统、修复后的影片，或丢失的数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stained glass laid flat on trestles, seventeen blue shards being fitted back into place under a lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：彩窗玻璃平放在木架上，十七块蓝色碎片在灯下被一片片放回原位。

branches.en: MATERIAL REPAIR: a building or artwork mended, and the cleaned version that results.
branches.cn: 物质修复：被修好的建筑或艺术品，以及由此产生的清理版本。

branches.en: POLITICAL ORDER PUT BACK: public order re-established, and a dynasty returned to power.
branches.cn: 政治秩序放回原处：公共秩序重建，王朝重新掌权。

branches.en: THE UNDOING OF A TAKING: property and archives returned to their owners.
branches.cn: 撤销一次夺取：财产与档案物归原主。

branches.en: THE BODY REPAIRED: health and strength slowly regained.
branches.cn: 身体被修好：健康与体力慢慢恢复。

branches.en: SYSTEMS RECOVERED: a degraded ecosystem and a failed disk both restored to function.
branches.cn: 系统恢复：退化的生态系统与故障硬盘都被恢复到可用状态。

intro.en: Restoration is restore plus -ation. The family includes restorative and restorer, with -ative marking what strengthens and -er marking the person.
intro.cn: restoration 由 restore 加 -ation 构成。词族包括 restorative 与 restorer，其中 -ative 标记能增强之物，-er 标记人。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is restaurare, with instaurare as a relative. The second element is of uncertain origin, so only the secure parts are labelled.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 restaurare，instaurare 为同族词。第二个成分来源不确定，因此只标注可靠的部分。

items.example: Latin inscriptions record the restaurare of temples after fires.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁铭文记载火灾之后对神庙的修复。

items.example: The related verb appears in discussions of founding a festival.
items.exampleCN: 这个相关动词出现在关于创立节庆的讨论中。

items.meaning: to repair, bring back, or give back
items.example: Workers restored the facade stone by stone.
items.exampleCN: 工人一块石头一块石头地修复了立面。

items.meaning: the act or result of bringing something back
items.meaningCN: 使某物恢复的行为或结果
items.example: The restoration returned the hall to its 1890 appearance.
items.exampleCN: 修复使大厅恢复到一八九〇年的样子。

items.meaning: able to restore health or strength
items.meaningCN: 有恢复健康或体力作用的
items.example: A hot meal proved restorative after the long walk.
items.exampleCN: 长途步行后，一顿热饭很能恢复体力。

items.meaning: a person who repairs old buildings or artworks
items.meaningCN: 修复古建筑或艺术品的人
items.example: The restorer worked with a microscope and a scalpel.
items.exampleCN: 修复师用显微镜和解剖刀工作。

items.meaning: able to be repaired or brought back
items.example: The painting was damaged but still restorable.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画受损，但仍可修复。

items.meaning: a person who wants an earlier state of things brought back
items.example: Restorationists argued for the old voting rules.
items.exampleCN: 复古派主张恢复旧的投票规则。

items.meaning: an approach that refuses to rebuild an earlier state
items.example: The architects chose non-restoration and left the ruin visible.
items.exampleCN: 建筑师选择不复原，让废墟保持可见。

definition_zh: 国内生产总值（缩写）；以国内生产总值计量的经济规模
definition_en: the abbreviation for gross domestic product, the total value of final output produced inside a country in a period
core_image: 发布厅屏幕上跳出一行数字，记者们立刻把它当作这一年经济成绩的单子
scene: 发布厅的屏幕上跳出一行数字，记者们立刻把它当作这一年经济成绩的单子，标题也在几分钟内改好。 The quarterly GDP figure beat every forecast.
sceneCN: 这里 GDP 指「国内生产总值的缩写」（第 1 个义项：境内最终产出总值的简称）；句意为季度国内生产总值数字超出所有预测。图中可辨识物件：发布厅屏幕、记者席、改好的标题、季度报表。

pos.zh: 国内生产总值（缩写）

derivatives.zh: 国内生产总值平减指数

senses.title: The abbreviation itself
senses.definition: the three-letter short form of gross domestic product, used as a count noun in reporting
senses.definitionCN: gross domestic product 的三字母简写，在报道中作可数名词使用
senses.example: The quarterly GDP figure beat every forecast.
senses.exampleCN: 季度国内生产总值数字超出所有预测。
senses.why: An initialism takes the first letters of a fixed phrase, so the letters carry the whole phrase without repeating it.
senses.whyCN: 首字母缩略取固定短语的首字母，因此这几个字母就承载了整个短语，无须重复全称。

senses.title: The accounting scope
senses.definition: the particular scope of measurement the letters stand for: final output produced inside a border
senses.definitionCN: 这些字母所代表的特定度量范围：国境之内生产的最终产出
senses.example: GDP counts what is made inside the border, not what citizens earn abroad.
senses.exampleCN: GDP 计的是国境之内做出来的东西，而非公民在海外赚到的。
senses.why: Each letter fixes a boundary of the measure, and quoting the abbreviation still commits the speaker to those boundaries.
senses.whyCN: 每个字母都固定了度量的一条边界，引用这个缩写也就意味着接受这些边界。

senses.title: The size of an economy
senses.definition: the total as a shorthand for how large an economy is
senses.definitionCN: 把总数用作经济体有多大的简略说法
senses.example: By GDP the country is the fourth largest in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 按 GDP 计，该国是区域内第四大经济体。
senses.why: A single headline number is convenient for ranking, so the abbreviation comes to stand for size itself.
senses.whyCN: 单一的头条数字便于排名，于是这个缩写转而代表规模本身。

senses.title: Nominal GDP
senses.definition: the total valued at current prices, without adjusting for inflation
senses.definitionCN: 按现价估值、未剔除通胀影响的总量
senses.example: Nominal GDP rose even though output hardly changed.
senses.exampleCN: 名义 GDP 上升了，尽管产出几乎没变。
senses.why: The same headline figure can be computed on two price bases, and the adjective tells the reader which one is meant.
senses.whyCN: 同一个头条数字可以按两种价格基准计算，形容词告诉读者指的是哪一种。

senses.title: Real GDP
senses.definition: the total valued at constant prices, so that only changes in quantity show
senses.definitionCN: 按不变价格估值、从而只显示数量变化的总量
senses.example: Real GDP is the figure analysts compare across years.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士跨年比较的是实际 GDP。
senses.why: To compare years, price change must be held still, and real marks that adjustment.
senses.whyCN: 要比较不同年份，必须把价格变动固定住，real 标记这一调整。

senses.title: GDP per head
senses.definition: the total divided by population, used as a rough measure of average income
senses.definitionCN: 总量按人口平均分摊，用作平均收入的粗略度量
senses.example: GDP per head says more about living standards than the total does.
senses.exampleCN: 人均 GDP 比总量更能说明生活水平。
senses.why: A larger population can raise the total while leaving each person no better off, so the per-head version is standard.
senses.whyCN: 人口增加可以抬高总量而个人并未变好，因此人均版本是常规做法。

senses.title: The GDP growth rate
senses.definition: the percentage change in the total from one period to the next
senses.definitionCN: 总量从一个时期到下一个时期变化的百分数
senses.example: GDP growth slowed to one percent in the final quarter.
senses.exampleCN: GDP 增长在最后一个季度放缓至百分之一。
senses.why: Because the abbreviation names a quantity, it readily combines with growth to name the change in that quantity.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个缩写指一个数量，它很容易与 growth 组合，指该数量的变化。

senses.title: GDP as a policy target
senses.definition: the total treated as the chief aim of government, often criticized as growth for its own sake
senses.definitionCN: 被当作政府首要目标的总量，常被批评为为增长而增长
senses.example: The plan put GDP ahead of clean water and quiet streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这份规划把 GDP 排在清洁水源与安静街道之前。
senses.why: Once a number is published quarterly, it can be managed as a target, and the abbreviation then names an objective rather than a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个数字按季公布，它就能被当作目标来管理，这个缩写于是指一项追求而非一个统计量。

intro.en: GDP is an initialism of gross domestic product: G for gross, D for domestic, P for product. The phrase came together with national accounting in the 1930s and 1940s, and the letters soon became the ordinary name. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: GDP 是 gross domestic product 的首字母缩略：G 代表 gross，D 代表 domestic，P 代表 product。这个短语随 20 世纪三四十年代的国民核算成形，这几个字母很快成为日常名称。年代均为约数。

items.en: G stands for gross, from Old French gros and Late Latin grossus 'thick, coarse, large', meaning the whole before any deduction.
items.cn: G 代表 gross，出自古法语 gros 与晚期拉丁 grossus「厚、粗、大」，意为扣除之前的整体。

items.en: D stands for domestic, from Latin domesticus 'of the house', here meaning what is produced inside the country's own border.
items.cn: D 代表 domestic，出自拉丁 domesticus「家的」，此处指在本国国境之内生产的东西。

items.en: P stands for product, from Latin producere 'to lead forth', naming what is made rather than what is earned.
items.cn: P 代表 product，出自拉丁 producere「引出」，指被造出的东西而非被赚到的收入。

items.en: The full phrase was assembled with the national accounts of the 1930s and 1940s, when a single measure of total output was needed for policy.
items.cn: 全称是在 20 世纪三四十年代建立国民核算时组合起来的，当时政策需要单一的产出的度量。

items.en: The three letters spread through official reports and newspapers in the following decades and largely displaced the full phrase in everyday use.
items.cn: 此后数十年间，这三个字母通过官方报告与报纸传播，在日常使用中基本取代了全称。

items.en: Later combinations such as GDP growth, GDP per capita and GDP deflator show that the abbreviation now behaves like an ordinary noun.
items.cn: 后来的 GDP growth、GDP per capita、GDP deflator 等组合表明，这个缩写如今已像普通名词一样使用。

note.en: The first group holds abbreviations and measures that are constantly confused with GDP; the second holds phrases that name an economy's size in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 GDP 混淆的缩写与度量；第二组是用其他方式命名经济规模的说法。

entries.definition: Gross national product counts output by a country's residents wherever they are, including income from abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 国民生产总值按一国居民计算产出，不论他们在何处，包含海外收入。

entries.definition: Gross national income measures what residents earn; it is the income-side successor to GNP and not the same as GDP.
entries.definitionCN: 国民总收入衡量居民赚到的收入；是 GNP 的收入侧后继者，与 GDP 不同。

entries.definition: Net domestic product subtracts the depreciation of machinery, so it is smaller than GDP.
entries.definitionCN: 国内生产净值扣除机器折旧，因此小于 GDP。

entries.definition: The phrase the three letters abbreviate; official documents often use it on first mention.
entries.definitionCN: 这三个字母所缩写的全称；官方文件常在首次提及时使用。

entries.definition: What an economy produces, stated without the accounting conventions that GDP carries.
entries.definitionCN: 经济体生产出的东西，不带 GDP 所含的核算惯例。

entries.definition: Total incomes earned by residents; it approaches the same total from the other direction.
entries.definitionCN: 居民获得的总收入；从另一方向接近同一个总数。

entries.definition: A loose way of speaking about how large an economy is, for which GDP is the usual yardstick.
entries.definitionCN: 谈论经济体有多大的宽松说法，GDP 是其常用尺子。

entries.definition: The system of production and exchange itself; GDP is one number about it, not the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 生产与交换的系统本身；GDP 只是关于它的一个数字，而非它本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the three initials, the full phrase behind them and real fixed compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：三个首字母、其背后的全称与真实的固定组合，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: G for gross, D for domestic, P for product: three letters, three limits.
normal.cn: G 是 gross，D 是 domestic，P 是 product：三个字母，三重限定。

normal.en: The full form is gross domestic product; the letters simply take its initials.
normal.cn: 全称是 gross domestic product；这几个字母只是取其首字母。

normal.en: Fixed compounds: GDP growth, GDP per capita, GDP deflator, real GDP.
normal.cn: 固定组合：GDP growth、GDP per capita、GDP deflator、real GDP。

normal.en: Real GDP means constant prices; nominal GDP means current prices.
normal.cn: real GDP 指不变价格；nominal GDP 指现价。

normal.en: The measure belongs to the national accounts of the 1930s and 1940s.
normal.cn: 这个度量属于 20 世纪三四十年代的国民核算。

abstract.en: Picture a number flashing on a screen before anyone has read the report behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一个数字先跳出来，背后的报告还没人读过。

abstract.en: Picture a country's whole year compressed into one line of a table.
abstract.cn: 想象整个国家的一年被压成表格里的一行。

abstract.en: Picture a border drawn on a map, with only what happens inside counted.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画着国界，只计界内发生的事。

examples.en: GDP rose by two percent in the year after the new port opened.
examples.cn: 新港口启用后的一年里，GDP 上升了百分之二。

examples.en: Comparisons of GDP across countries depend on how prices are converted.
examples.cn: 跨国比较 GDP 取决于价格如何换算。

examples.en: The government was accused of chasing GDP while ignoring the rivers.
examples.cn: 政府被指责一味追逐 GDP 而无视河流的状况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「G（总）+ D（国内）+ P（产出）」——三个首字母合成一个国家的年度成绩单 → 国内生产总值

root: GDP 为 gross domestic product 的首字母缩略；gross 出古法语 gros／晚期拉丁 grossus（厚、粗，更早来源存疑），domestic 出拉丁 domesticus（domus 家），product 出拉丁 producere（pro- 向前 + ducere 引导）。缩略用法随 20 世纪国民核算普及。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one abbreviation: the three letters stand for a measured total, and that total is read as a scope, a size, a price basis, a share per head, a rate and finally a policy aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缩写展开：三个字母代表一个被度量的总数，这个总数再依次被读作核算范围、经济规模、价格基准、人均份额、一个比率，最后是一项政策目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number flashing on a press-room screen, taken as the country's report card for the year.
core.cn: 核心意象：发布厅屏幕上一个跳出的数字，被当作这个国家一年的成绩单。

branches.en: LETTERS AND SCOPE: the initials carry a phrase, and the phrase fixes what is counted and where.
branches.cn: 字母与范围：首字母承载一个短语，而短语固定了计什么、计哪里。

branches.en: SIZE AND CURRENT PRICES: a headline total ranks economies, and at current prices it swells with inflation.
branches.cn: 规模与现价：头条总数给经济体排名，而按现价它会随通胀膨胀。

branches.en: CONSTANT PRICES AND PER HEAD: the total is adjusted for price change and then divided among people.
branches.cn: 不变价与人均：总数先按价格变动调整，再分到人头上。

branches.en: RATE: the same total becomes a percentage change from one period to the next.
branches.cn: 比率：同一个总数变成相邻时期变化的百分数。

branches.en: AIM: a published statistic turns into something a government is expected to deliver.
branches.cn: 目标：一个公布的统计量变成政府被要求交付的东西。

intro.en: This entry is an initialism, so its parts are three letters rather than prefixes and suffixes; the letters in turn stand for words with their own roots.
intro.cn: 这一条是首字母缩略，因此它的构成是三个字母，而不是前缀与后缀；这三个字母又分别代表有自己词根的词。

latinIntro.en: The letters abbreviate gross, domestic and product, whose roots are Late Latin grossus, Latin domus and Latin producere; the abbreviation itself has no Latin form.
latinIntro.cn: 这三个字母缩写的是 gross、domestic 与 product，其词根分别为晚期拉丁 grossus、拉丁 domus 与拉丁 producere；缩写本身没有拉丁形式。

items.example: The letter carries the first limit of the measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个字母承载度量的第一重限定。

items.example: The letter fixes the border of the count.
items.exampleCN: 这个字母固定计数的边界。

items.example: The letter names the thing measured.
items.exampleCN: 这个字母命名被度量的对象。

items.example: Gross output is counted before wear and tear.
items.exampleCN: 总产出在磨损扣除之前计算。

items.example: Domestic output excludes what is made abroad.
items.exampleCN: 国内产出不含在国外制造的东西。

items.example: The product measure counts final goods only.
items.exampleCN: 产出度量只计最终商品。

items.example: The suffix marks the adjective of the house.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记「家的」这一形容词。

items.meaning: the short name of the measure
items.example: The initialism behaves like an ordinary noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个首字母缩略像普通名词一样使用。
