definition_zh: 过度捕捞；捕捞超过可持续产量；生长型过度捕捞；补充型过度捕捞；经济型过度捕捞；生态系统型过度捕捞
definition_en: fishing at a rate that removes fish faster than the population can replace them
core_image: 渔网从海里拉起，网眼里的鱼越来越小、越来越少
scene: 清晨的码头上，渔民把一网小鱼倒进筐里，最大的也不过手掌长。 Biologists warn that overfishing has emptied the grounds their grandparents knew.
sceneCN: 这里指「捕捞速度超过鱼类自我补充能力」（第 1 个义项：从种群中取走的鱼多于其繁殖补充的总过程）；句意为生物学家警告，过度捕捞已经掏空了祖辈熟悉的老渔场。场景物件：渔网、小鱼、鱼筐、码头。

pos.zh: 过度捕捞（不可数；作动名词用）

collocations.zh: 对某一种群的过度捕捞

forms.label: 相关形容词（已被过度捕捞的）
相关名词（渔业；渔场，复数）

senses.title: Fishing beyond replacement
senses.definition: fishing at a rate that removes fish faster than the population can replace them
senses.definitionCN: 捕走鱼的速度快于种群繁殖补充的速度
senses.example: Biologists warn that overfishing has emptied the grounds their grandparents knew.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家警告，过度捕捞已经掏空了祖辈熟悉的老渔场。
senses.why: Over- marks excess and fishing marks the taking, so the word is the simple idea of taking more than the stock can give back.
senses.whyCN: over- 标记过量，fishing 标记捕取，因此这个词就是「取得比资源能还回来的更多」这一简单观念。

senses.title: Growth overfishing
senses.definition: taking fish so young that the stock loses the yield it would have gained if they had grown
senses.definitionCN: 捕走太幼小的鱼，使资源失去它们长大本可带来的产量
senses.example: Growth overfishing shows up as smaller fish in every catch.
senses.exampleCN: 生长型过度捕捞表现为每网鱼都更小。
senses.why: Fisheries science splits the problem by mechanism, and this first type is about individual growth rather than births.
senses.whyCN: 渔业科学按机制拆分问题，这第一种关于个体生长，而不是出生。

senses.title: Recruitment overfishing
senses.definition: taking so many adults that too few remain to produce the next generation
senses.definitionCN: 捕走太多成鱼，剩下的个体不足以繁殖下一代
senses.example: Recruitment overfishing leaves too few spawners for a good year class.
senses.exampleCN: 补充型过度捕捞留下的产卵鱼太少，难以形成好年级群。
senses.why: The second type attacks the birth side of the equation, so the stock loses its capacity to recruit new fish.
senses.whyCN: 第二种类型打击等式出生的一端，资源因此失去补充新鱼的能力。

senses.title: Economic overfishing
senses.definition: keeping more fishing capacity than the stock can support profitably
senses.definitionCN: 保有的捕捞能力超过资源能有利可图支撑的水平
senses.example: Economic overfishing persists even when catch limits are set.
senses.exampleCN: 即使设定了捕捞上限，经济型过度捕捞仍然存在。
senses.why: Boats can chase too few fish because subsidies and competition keep them at sea, so the problem is economic as well as biological.
senses.whyCN: 补贴与竞争让船继续出海，去追已经太少的鱼，因此问题既是生物性的，也是经济性的。

senses.title: Ecosystem overfishing
senses.definition: fishing that alters the balance of species and food webs, not just the target stock
senses.definitionCN: 改变物种平衡与食物网、而不只影响目标种群的捕捞
senses.example: Ecosystem overfishing removed the large predators first.
senses.exampleCN: 生态系统型过度捕捞先移除了大型捕食者。
senses.why: When the catch reshapes the whole community, the word widens from one stock to the system.
senses.whyCN: 当捕捞重塑整个群落，这个词就从单一资源扩展到整个系统。

senses.title: Stock collapse
senses.definition: the end state in which a stock falls so low that the fishery can no longer operate
senses.definitionCN: 资源低到渔业无法再运作的终局状态
senses.example: Overfishing brought the cod stock to collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 过度捕捞把鳕鱼资源推向崩溃。
senses.why: Because the process has a visible endpoint, the word often stands for the collapse it causes.
senses.whyCN: 因为这一过程有可见的终点，这个词常直接指它造成的崩溃。

senses.title: A policy target
senses.definition: the problem that catch limits, subsidies reform and closed seasons are meant to solve
senses.definitionCN: 捕捞上限、补贴改革与禁渔期旨在解决的问题
senses.example: The plan aims to end overfishing by a fixed date.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划目标是在既定日期前终止过度捕捞。
senses.why: Once the process was measured, it became something governments could legislate against.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个过程可测量，它就变成政府可以立法应对的对象。

senses.title: Figurative over-extraction
senses.definition: taking more from any limited resource than it can renew
senses.definitionCN: 从任何有限资源中取走超过其再生能力的东西
senses.example: The startup suffered overfishing of its best engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司对最优秀工程师的「过度捕捞」使其受损。
senses.why: The fishing image is easy to borrow for any finite pool of talent or attention, so the word can leave the sea.
senses.whyCN: 捕鱼的意象很容易借给任何有限的人才或注意力池，因此这个词可以离开海洋。

intro.en: Overfishing joins the native prefix over- 'too much' to fishing, whose root fish descends from Old English fisc and Germanic *fiskaz. The compound is modern resource science. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: overfishing 把本族前缀 over-「过多」与 fishing 组合，后者的词根 fish 出自古英语 fisc 与日耳曼语 *fiskaz。这个复合词属现代资源科学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ofer 'over, beyond' is the native source of over-, marking excess or going beyond a limit.
items.cn: ofer「在上、超过」是 over- 的本族来源，标记过量或越界。

items.en: Fisc 'fish' descends from Germanic *fiskaz, a reconstructed form related to Latin piscis.
items.cn: fisc「鱼」出自日耳曼语 *fiskaz，此为重构形式，与拉丁 piscis 同源。

items.en: The gerund fishing names the activity of catching fish; it is formed from the verb fish plus -ing.
items.cn: 动名词 fishing 指捕鱼活动，由动词 fish 加 -ing 构成。

items.en: Overfishing became a technical term in twentieth-century fisheries science, once catch statistics could be compared with stock growth.
items.cn: 二十世纪渔业科学能把渔获统计与资源生长相比较之后，overfishing 成为技术术语。

items.en: Later work split the idea into growth, recruitment, economic and ecosystem overfishing, each naming a different failure.
items.cn: 后来的研究把它拆成生长型、补充型、经济型与生态系统型，每种各指一种不同的失灵。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic source of *fiskaz is not settled, and the first use of overfishing in its modern technical sense is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：*fiskaz 在日耳曼语之前的来源无定论，overfishing 现代技术义的最早使用没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds same-root fish and fishery forms; group two holds related catch and depletion terms that are not synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是同根 fish 与 fishery 形式；第二组是相关但并非同义的捕捞与枯竭术语。

entries.definition: To fish a stock too hard; the verb names the act, while overfishing names the process and its state.
entries.definitionCN: 把资源捕得太狠；动词指行为，overfishing 指过程与状态。

entries.definition: Describing a stock already reduced below safe limits; it is the condition, not the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 描述资源已被压到安全线以下；它是状态，不是活动。

entries.definition: Catching fish in general; overfishing adds that the rate is beyond replacement.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指捕鱼；overfishing 追加了「超过补充速度」这一层。

entries.definition: A stock, ground or industry; it is what overfishing damages, not the damage itself.
entries.definitionCN: 资源、渔场或产业；它是过度捕捞损害的对象，而不是损害本身。

entries.definition: Taking any wild resource beyond renewal; it can apply to forests and plants, while overfishing is marine and fish-specific.
entries.definitionCN: 取走任何野生资源超过其再生；可用于森林与植物，而过度捕捞专指鱼类与海洋。

entries.definition: Non-target animals caught accidentally; it is a separate harm that often accompanies overfishing.
entries.definitionCN: 意外捕到的非目标动物；它是常与过度捕捞并行的另一种危害。

entries.definition: The reduction of a fish stock; it is the outcome that overfishing produces.
entries.definitionCN: 鱼类资源的减少；它是过度捕捞造成的结果。

entries.definition: The catch a stock can give year after year; overfishing is fishing above that limit.
entries.definitionCN: 资源年复一年能提供的渔获；过度捕捞就是超过这一上限。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real native parts, real fisheries categories and real management collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实本族构件、真实渔业类别与真实管理搭配。

normal.en: Over- means too much; fishing means taking fish.
normal.cn: over- 是太多，fishing 是捕鱼。

normal.en: The four subtypes are growth, recruitment, economic and ecosystem.
normal.cn: 四个子类是生长型、补充型、经济型与生态系统型。

normal.en: Fish is fisc in Old English, related to Latin piscis.
normal.cn: fish 在古英语是 fisc，与拉丁 piscis 同源。

normal.en: Bycatch is a separate problem that often travels with overfishing.
normal.cn: 兼捕是与过度捕捞常同行的另一个问题。

normal.en: The fix is a catch limit set below sustainable yield.
normal.cn: 解决办法是把捕捞上限设在可持续产量之下。

abstract.en: Picture a net coming up with smaller and smaller fish each season.
abstract.cn: 想象每一季拉上来的网里，鱼越来越小。

abstract.en: Picture a bank account emptied faster than interest can refill it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账户，取钱快过利息回填。

abstract.en: Picture a food web losing its top strand first.
abstract.cn: 想象一张食物网先失去最上面那股线。

examples.en: Overfishing removed the oldest and largest fish first.
examples.cn: 过度捕捞先移走最老最大的鱼。

examples.en: Subsidies can keep overfishing profitable for a while.
examples.cn: 补贴能让过度捕捞在一段时间内仍有利可图。

examples.en: The stock recovered only after overfishing was ended.
examples.cn: 资源只有在过度捕捞终止后才恢复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「over（过度）+ fishing（捕鱼）」——捕得比鱼能补回来的更多 → 过度捕捞

root: over- 出自古英语 ofer「在上、超过」；fish 出自古英语 fisc，属日耳曼语 *fiskaz（重构形式），与拉丁 piscis 同源；加 -ing 构成动名词。现代技术义形成于二十世纪渔业科学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one excess: taking beyond replacement, the growth type, the recruitment type, the economic type, the ecosystem type, collapse, policy, and any over-extraction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种「过量」展开：超过补充、生长型、补充型、经济型、生态系统型、崩溃、政策，以及任何过度索取。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a net hauled up full of small fish that never had time to grow.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉上来的网里全是还没来得及长大的小鱼。

branches.en: RATE TO SIZE: taking too many small fish is the first way the rate shows up.
branches.cn: 从速度到体型：捕走太多小鱼，是这一速度最先显现的方式。

branches.en: BIRTH TO COLLAPSE: too few spawners is how a stock loses its next generation and then its fishery.
branches.cn: 从出生到崩溃：产卵鱼太少，资源先失去下一代，再失去渔业。

branches.en: PROFIT TO POLICY: subsidies keep excess capacity alive, so reform must change the economics.
branches.cn: 从利润到政策：补贴让过剩产能存活，改革必须改变经济账。

branches.en: THE ECOSYSTEM: catch the whole food web and collapse becomes hard to reverse.
branches.cn: 生态系统：捕空整张食物网，崩溃就更难逆转。

branches.en: OVER-EXTRACTION METAPHOR: any finite pool can be fished too hard, including talent.
branches.cn: 过度索取比喻：任何有限的池子都可能被捕得太狠，包括人才。

intro.en: Overfishing is a native prefix plus a gerund; there is no borrowed affix, and the meaning is the sum of its two visible parts.
intro.cn: overfishing 由本族前缀加动名词构成；没有借来词缀，意义就是两个可见部分之和。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer appears only through the distant relative piscis 'fish'; the word itself is native English and Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层只通过远亲 piscis「鱼」出现；这个词本身属英语本族与日耳曼语。

items.example: Over- turns a normal action into an excess.
items.exampleCN: over- 把正常动作变成过量。

items.example: They fish the same bank every spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年春天在同一片滩捕鱼。
船队过度捕捞共享资源。

items.meaningCN: 已被捕到安全线以下的
items.example: The overfished bank closed for a year.
items.exampleCN: 过度捕捞的渔场关闭了一年。

items.meaning: the process of fishing beyond replacement
items.meaningCN: 超过补充速度的捕捞过程
items.example: Overfishing is the main cause of collapse.
items.exampleCN: 过度捕捞是资源崩溃的主要原因。

items.example: The fishery employs three hundred people.

items.meaningCN: 意外捕到的非目标动物
items.example: Bycatch includes turtles and young fish.

items.meaning: the catch that can be taken year after year
items.example: The limit is set below sustainable yield.
items.exampleCN: 上限设在可持续产量之下。

definition_zh: 萌发；发芽；开始生长
definition_en: the beginning of growth in a seed or spore, especially the moment it breaks out of its coat
core_image: 一粒种子吸水膨胀，白色的胚根顶破种皮，伸进湿土
scene: 培养箱里，一排培养皿放在恒温架上，第七天早晨其中几粒种子先后裂开。 Germination began on the seventh day, when the first radicle broke through the coat.
sceneCN: 这里 germination 指「萌发」（第 1 个义项：胚根突破种皮开始生长）；句意为萌发在第七天开始，第一支胚根突破了种皮。

pos.zh: 萌发；发芽；萌发过程

senses.title: Breaking out of the seed coat
senses.definition: the first visible step of growth, when the young root emerges from the seed
senses.definitionCN: 生长的第一个可见步骤，幼根从种子中伸出
senses.example: Germination is complete once the radicle has emerged.
senses.exampleCN: 胚根一旦伸出，萌发就完成了。
senses.why: the word marks a threshold rather than a gradual process: something enclosed becomes something exposed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的是一个门槛，而不是渐进过程：被包住的东西变成暴露的东西。

senses.title: The uptake of water that starts it
senses.definition: the swelling that follows water uptake and precedes visible growth
senses.definitionCN: 吸水之后、可见生长之前的膨胀
senses.example: Germination begins with imbibition, long before any root appears.
senses.exampleCN: 萌发从吸胀开始，远在根出现之前。
senses.why: water is the switch, so the same noun is used for the hidden stage that makes the visible stage possible.
senses.whyCN: 水是开关，因此同一个名词也用于那个使可见阶段成为可能的隐藏阶段。

senses.title: The rate at which seeds sprout
senses.definition: the proportion or speed of seeds that successfully sprout in a batch
senses.definitionCN: 一批种子中成功发芽的比例或速度
senses.example: Cold storage lowered the germination rate to sixty percent.
senses.exampleCN: 冷藏把发芽率降到了六成。
senses.why: a mass process needs a number, so the noun becomes the measurable quantity rather than the single event.
senses.whyCN: 群体过程需要一个数，因此名词变成可计量的量，而不只是单次事件。

senses.title: A test of seed quality
senses.definition: a standard procedure for counting how many seeds in a sample sprout
senses.definitionCN: 统计样本中有多少种子发芽的标准程序
senses.example: The lab runs a germination test before the lot is sold.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在出售这批种子之前做发芽试验。
senses.why: the process is turned into an industrial check, so the noun names the procedure itself.
senses.whyCN: 这一过程被变成工业检验，因此名词命名的是程序本身。

senses.title: Sprouting of a spore
senses.definition: the emergence of a growth tube from a fungal, fern or moss spore
senses.definitionCN: 真菌、蕨或苔藓的孢子伸出生长管
senses.example: Spore germination requires a damp film on the leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 孢子萌发需要叶面有一层水膜。
senses.why: spores use the same threshold as seeds, so the botanical noun is borrowed for them unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 孢子与种子跨过同样的门槛，因此植物学的名词原样借用于它们。

senses.title: Pollen tube growth on a stigma
senses.definition: the growth of a pollen tube after a grain lands on a compatible stigma
senses.definitionCN: 花粉落到亲和的柱头后长出花粉管
senses.example: Pollen germination fails on a stigma of the wrong species.
senses.exampleCN: 花粉落到异种柱头上时萌发失败。
senses.why: the grain behaves like a seed on soil, so the term travels to the flower's receiving surface.
senses.whyCN: 花粉粒在柱头上的表现如同种子落在土上，这个词因此移到花的接受面。

senses.title: Sprouting after dormancy ends
senses.definition: the resumption of growth once a dormant seed's block is removed
senses.definitionCN: 休眠种子的阻碍被解除后重新开始生长
senses.example: Scarifying the coat synchronised germination across the batch.
senses.exampleCN: 划破种皮使整批种子同步萌发。
senses.why: dormancy is defined as the absence of germination, so the noun also names what happens when the absence ends.
senses.whyCN: 休眠被定义为「不萌发」，因此名词也命名这种缺席结束时所发生的事。

senses.title: Metaphor: an idea beginning to grow
senses.definition: figurative, the first stage of an idea or plan becoming active
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指想法或计划开始活跃的第一阶段
senses.example: The germination of the project took a year of quiet conversations.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目的萌生用了一年安静的交谈。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the threshold image: something small and enclosed becomes visible and growing.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留门槛意象：小而封闭的东西变得可见并开始生长。

intro.en: Germination is the noun of germinate, from Latin germinare 'to sprout', built on germen 'sprout, bud, seed'. The deeper origin of germen is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: germination 是 germinate 的名词，来自拉丁 germinare「发芽」，建立在 germen「芽、胚、种子」之上。germen 的更早来源不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Germen meant 'sprout, bud, offshoot, seed'; it named the living point from which a plant extends.
items.cn: germen 意为「芽、幼枝、种子」；它命名的是一株植物向外伸展的那个活的起点。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin ancestry of germen is not established; the link to a root meaning 'to produce, beget' is a common reconstruction rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：germen 在拉丁语之前的谱系未得证明；把它连到意为「产生、生育」的词根，是常见的重构，而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Germinare 'to sprout, bud' gave the verb whose noun is germinatio.
items.cn: germinare「发芽、抽芽」提供了动词，其名词形式为 germinatio。

items.en: English germinate is recorded in the seventeenth century, and germination follows as its noun.
items.cn: 英语 germinate 自 17 世纪有记录，germination 随之成为其名词。

items.en: Seed-testing laboratories in the nineteenth century made germination a measured quantity rather than a single observed event.
items.cn: 19 世纪的种子检验实验室把萌发变成可计量的量，而不只是一次观察到的个别事件。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest printed use of germination is not firmly dated, so the seventeenth-century placement is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：germination 最早见于印刷的时间没有确证，因此归于 17 世纪只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates the germ- words that look alike; group two separates the start of growth from the stages that follow or precede it.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形相近的 germ- 系词；第二组区分生长的开始与其前后阶段。

entries.definition: To sprout; the verb is what the seed does, the noun is what happens.
entries.definitionCN: 发芽；动词是种子所做的，名词是所发生的事。

entries.definition: The embryo inside a seed, or a disease-causing microbe; the shared root means 'sprout', not 'disease'.
entries.definitionCN: 种子内的胚，或致病微生物；共同词根意为「芽」，并非「疾病」。

entries.definition: Relating to a germ or to an early stage; it describes a stage, not the act of sprouting.
entries.definitionCN: 与胚或早期阶段有关；描述阶段，而非发芽的动作。

entries.definition: The name of a people and a language, unrelated to germen despite the spelling; it comes from Latin Germanus.
entries.definitionCN: 民族与语言的名称，尽管拼写相似，却与 germen 无关；它来自拉丁 Germanus。

entries.definition: The common word for a shoot appearing; germination is the technical term for the same threshold, extended to spores and pollen.
entries.definitionCN: 嫩芽出现的日常说法；germination 是同一门槛的术语说法，并扩展到孢子与花粉。

entries.definition: The fusion of gametes, which in flowering plants precedes germination of the resulting seed.
entries.definitionCN: 配子的融合；在开花植物中，它先于由此形成的种子萌发。

entries.definition: The state in which a seed will not sprout even when conditions seem right; germination is what dormancy blocks.
entries.definitionCN: 即使条件看似合适种子也不发芽的状态；萌发正是休眠所阻止的事。

entries.definition: The seedling's appearance above the soil surface, a later and separate event from germination underground.
entries.definitionCN: 幼苗露出土面，是萌发之后另一个独立事件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real root, the seed-testing phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、种子检验搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: germen 'sprout' + -ation: the sprouting, named as a process.
normal.cn: germen「芽」+ -ation：把发芽这件事作为过程来命名。

normal.en: The same root gives germ, germinate, germinal.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 germ、germinate、germinal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: germination rate, germination test, spore germination.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：发芽率、发芽试验、孢子萌发。

normal.en: The threshold is visible: nothing shows until the radicle breaks through.
normal.cn: 门槛是可见的：胚根突破之前什么也看不见。

normal.en: Water starts it; dormancy delays it; scarifying synchronises it.
normal.cn: 水启动它，休眠推迟它，划破种皮让它同步。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed packet that splits along one seam and lets light in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个密封的包裹沿一条缝裂开，光透了进来。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation so quiet that nobody notices until a plan exists.
abstract.cn: 想象一场安静的交谈，直到计划成形才有人注意到。

abstract.en: Picture a dormant field that turns green within a week of the first rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一片休眠的田，在初雨之后一周内变绿。

examples.en: Germination was uneven because the seed lot was old.
examples.cn: 由于种子批次陈旧，萌发参差不齐。

examples.en: The germination test showed ninety percent viability.
examples.cn: 发芽试验显示九成的存活率。

examples.en: Pollen germination on the stigma takes about six hours.
examples.cn: 花粉在柱头上萌发约需六小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「germ（芽）+ ination」——芽从种皮里冒出来 → 萌发

root: 拉丁 germen, germinis「芽、胚、种子」→ germinare「发芽」→ germinatio → 英语 germination。germen 的更早来源不确定，与「产生、生育」词根的联系属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of germination follow one threshold: something enclosed takes in water, swells, and breaks out, whether it is a seed, a spore, a pollen grain or an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: germination 的八个义项跨过同一个门槛：封闭之物吸水、膨胀、破壳而出，无论那是种子、孢子、花粉粒还是一个想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale root pushing through a split coat into wet soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支白色的根从裂开的种皮里顶出，伸进湿土。

branches.en: THE THRESHOLD: invisible swelling turns into a visible break.
branches.cn: 门槛：看不见的膨胀变成看得见的突破。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: a batch is counted, so the event becomes a rate and a test.
branches.cn: 数字：对一批种子计数，事件因此变成比率与试验。

branches.en: OTHER BODIES: spores and pollen grains cross the same threshold.
branches.cn: 其他个体：孢子与花粉粒跨过同一门槛。

branches.en: THE BLOCK REMOVED: dormancy is defined by the absence of this event.
branches.cn: 阻碍解除：休眠正以这件事的缺席来定义。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: a plan can swell and break out too.
branches.cn: 比喻：计划也会膨胀并破壳。

intro.en: Germination is a Latin root plus a noun suffix, and the family covers both the living point and the act of emerging from it.
intro.cn: germination 是拉丁词根加名词后缀，其词族既覆盖那个活的起点，也覆盖从它冒出的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin germen 'sprout' yields germinare and germinatio; English draws germ, germinate, germination, germinal and germinative from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 germen「芽」衍生 germinare 与 germinatio；英语的 germ、germinate、germination、germinal 与 germinative 都取自同一词族。

items.example: The root names the point of new growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名新生的起点。

items.example: Germination names the process of sprouting.

items.meaning: embryo of a seed; a microbe
items.example: The germ is the living point inside the seed.
items.exampleCN: 胚是种子内部那个活的起点。

items.example: The seeds germinate within a week.
The germinative capacity fell after storage.
items.exampleCN: 贮藏之后发芽能力下降。

items.meaning: relating to a germ or early stage
items.example: The idea was still germinal at that meeting.
items.exampleCN: 那次会上这个想法仍处初期。
发芽能力随收获日期而变化。

items.meaning: the share of seeds that sprout
items.example: The germination rate was recorded after ten days.

definition_zh: 海岸的；沿海的；沿岸的；海岸带的
definition_en: relating to the coast, the land along the edge of the sea, or to the strip where land and sea meet
core_image: 一条窄窄的陆带贴着海走，内侧是农田与公路，外侧是不断拍岸的白浪
scene: 公路沿着盐沼与沙丘之间的低地延伸，尽头是一座渡口。 The road ran through coastal marsh and dune before it reached the ferry.
sceneCN: 这里 coastal 指「沿海的、位于海岸边的」（第 2 个义项：坐落在海岸边或沿海地带的）；句意：公路穿过沿海的盐沼与沙丘，最后到达渡口。图中可辨识物件：盐沼水面、白色沙丘、贴着岸线的公路、渡口栈桥。

pos.zh: 海岸的；沿海的；沿岸的（位于海岸或与海岸有关的）
海岸带的（涉及其生态、工程、管理与规划的）

derivatives.zh: 海岸；沿海地区 / 沿岸航行；（车）滑行
海岸线（整条岸线的走向与轮廓）
沿海航船；杯垫（在桌面滑行的垫片）
海岸警卫队；海岸巡防人员

senses.title: Of the coast
senses.titleCN: 海岸的、与海岸有关的（总义）
senses.definition: relating to the coast, the margin of land that borders the sea
senses.definitionCN: 指与海岸有关的，即与陆地临海边缘有关
senses.example: Coastal roads flood at every spring tide.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢大潮，沿海公路都会积水。
senses.why: the suffix -al makes a relational adjective out of coast, so the word simply says 'having to do with the coast'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把 coast 变成关系形容词，这个词的基本意思就是「与海岸有关的」。

senses.title: Situated on the shore
senses.titleCN: 沿海的、坐落在海岸边的
senses.definition: situated on or along the shore, as a town, road or plain
senses.definitionCN: 指位于海岸之上或沿海岸延伸的，如城镇、公路、平原
senses.example: Coastal towns grew quickly after the railway arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路通了以后，沿海城镇迅速发展起来。
senses.why: this is the local reading: the adjective marks position relative to the sea, not a subject matter.
senses.whyCN: 这是位置义：形容词标记相对于海的位置，而不是某个主题。

senses.title: Coastal ecology
senses.titleCN: 海岸生态的（盐沼、红树、沙丘等生境）
senses.definition: of the habitats where land and sea meet, such as salt marsh, mangrove, dune and rock pool
senses.definitionCN: 指陆海相接处的生境，如盐沼、红树林、沙丘与岩池
senses.example: Coastal wetlands filter runoff before it reaches the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸湿地在径流入海之前将其过滤。
senses.why: the same adjective now qualifies habitats rather than places, because ecology treats that strip as a distinct system.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词现在修饰生境而非地点，因为生态学把这条窄带视为独特系统。

senses.title: Coastal engineering and defence
senses.definition: of structures built to hold or protect the shore, such as sea walls, groynes, breakwaters and revetments
senses.definitionCN: 指为固定或保护海岸而建的构筑物，如海堤、丁坝、防波堤与护坡
senses.example: Coastal defences failed during the winter storm.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季风暴期间，海岸防护设施失效。
senses.why: once people build against the sea, the adjective attaches to the works rather than to the land.
senses.whyCN: 人们一旦对着海建造，这个形容词便附着于工程物而非陆地。

senses.title: Coastal communities and economy
senses.titleCN: 沿海居民与沿海经济的
senses.definition: of the people, work and income that depend on the shore, such as fishing, shipping and tourism
senses.definitionCN: 指依赖海岸的人、生计与收入，如渔业、航运与旅游
senses.example: Coastal economies depend on both fishing and visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海经济同时依赖渔业与游客。
senses.why: from the place the adjective passes to the people in it: a coastal town is also a town whose living comes from the sea.
senses.whyCN: 形容词由地点过渡到地点上的人：沿海城镇同时也是靠海为生的城镇。

senses.title: Alongshore navigation
senses.titleCN: 沿岸航行的、近岸水域的
senses.definition: of sailing or shipping that keeps close to land, in the belt of water near the shore
senses.definitionCN: 指贴近陆地航行，或在近岸水带中营运的航运
senses.example: Coastal shipping declined once the motorway opened.
senses.exampleCN: 高速公路通车后，沿岸航运衰落了。
senses.why: the nautical sense keeps the original 'side' idea: the ship works along the edge of the land, not across open sea.
senses.whyCN: 航海义保留了原初的「侧边」意念：船沿着陆地边缘航行，而非横穿外海。

senses.title: Coastal zone management
senses.titleCN: 海岸带管理的（政策与规划义）
senses.definition: of the planning, law and policy that govern the strip where sea and land interact
senses.definitionCN: 指管理陆海相互作用地带的规划、法律与政策
senses.example: Coastal management balances building, farming and habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸带管理在建设、农业与生境之间取得平衡。
senses.why: administration turns the physical strip into a jurisdiction, so the adjective comes to name a field of rules.
senses.whyCN: 行政管理把这条实体窄带变成管辖对象，这个形容词因而指一个规则领域。

senses.title: Coastal climate
senses.titleCN: 沿海气候的、受海岸影响的
senses.definition: of the weather of the shore, shaped by sea breeze and by the sea's slow change of temperature
senses.definitionCN: 指海岸地带的天气，受海风与海水缓慢变温影响
senses.example: Coastal air stays cooler than inland air in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季沿海空气比内陆空气凉爽。
senses.why: the sea beside the land moderates it, so the adjective can describe air as well as ground.
senses.whyCN: 紧邻陆地的海对陆地起调节作用，因此这个形容词也能形容空气而不只是地面。

intro.en: Coastal is coast plus the relational suffix -al. Coast reached English through Old French coste from Latin costa 'rib, side'; the 'shore' sense developed in the Romance languages from the idea of a flank or side. The adjective itself is recorded from the early nineteenth century, and the deeper origin of costa is unsettled.
intro.cn: coastal 是 coast 加关系后缀 -al。coast 经古法语 coste 来自拉丁 costa「肋骨、侧面」；「海岸」义在罗曼语族中由「侧边、侧面」的意思发展而来。该形容词本身在 19 世纪初见于记载，而 costa 的更深来源尚无定论。

items.en: Costa meant 'rib' and, by extension, 'side or wall'; the shore reading is not the classical core but grew later out of 'side, edge'.
items.cn: costa 意为「肋骨」，并引申为「侧面、壁」；「海岸」义并非古典时期的核心义，而是后来由「侧边、边缘」发展出来的。

items.en: Old French coste carried both 'rib' and 'side, slope, shore'; this is the form English borrowed, and Italian costa shows the same shift.
items.cn: 古法语 coste 同时有「肋骨」与「侧面、坡、岸」两义；英语借入的就是这个形式，意大利语 costa 也呈现同样的词义转移。

items.en: English coast is recorded in the fourteenth century for the land edge by the sea, and the verb 'to sail along a coast' follows from it.
items.cn: 英语 coast 在 14 世纪以「临海陆缘」义见于记载，动词「沿岸航行」由此派生。

items.en: The Latin suffix -alis, through French -al, makes relational adjectives; coast plus -al yields the plain meaning 'of the coast'.
items.cn: 拉丁后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 构成关系形容词；coast 加 -al 就得到「海岸的」这一基本意思。

items.en: Coastal is recorded in the early nineteenth century, when coastal survey, coastal trade and coastal defence became routine terms of administration and commerce.
items.cn: coastal 在 19 世纪初见于记载，当时海岸测量、沿岸贸易与海岸防护已成为行政与商业的常用说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of costa and first date of coastal): the pre-Latin form of costa is not established, and any suggested root is a reconstruction; the earliest citation of coastal is only approximately dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（costa 的更深词源与 coastal 的首见年代）：costa 的拉丁语之前形式未得到证明，所拟词根均属重构形式；coastal 的最早书证只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike or homophonous words: costal and coastal share one Latin root but went opposite ways, while coast, coastline and coaster are built on the same base. Group two holds true near-synonyms that differ in register or in what part of the edge they name.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或同音词：costal 与 coastal 共用同一个拉丁词根却走向不同，coast、coastline、coaster 则同出一个基础词。第二组是真近义词，差别在语体或所指的岸的哪一部分。

entries.definition: Of the ribs, as in costal cartilage; it is cognate with coastal through Latin costa, but it kept the anatomical sense and never means 'shore'.
entries.definitionCN: 指肋骨的，如肋软骨；它经拉丁 costa 与 coastal 同源，但保留了解剖义，从不表示「海岸」。

entries.definition: The shore itself, and the verb 'to sail along it' or 'to move without power'; same root as coastal, but a noun or verb rather than an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指海岸本身，也指「沿岸航行」或「滑行」的动词；与 coastal 同根，但为名词或动词而非形容词。

entries.definition: The coast considered as a line, especially its shape on a map or over a long stretch; same base, but a compound noun with a geometric image.
entries.definitionCN: 指被看作一条线的海岸，尤其地图上或长距离上的走向；基础词相同，但为带几何意象的复合名词。

entries.definition: A ship that trades along a coast, or a small mat that slides on a table; same root, but it names an object, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿岸贸易的船，或桌上滑动的杯垫；词根相同，但指具体物件而非性质。

entries.definition: Of the shore zone between high and low water and just beyond it; it is the technical ecology term, coastal being the general one.
entries.definitionCN: 指高低潮之间及其外侧的滨岸带；是生态学的术语，coastal 则是通称。

entries.definition: Of the sea in relation to shipping, trade and law; it stresses activity at sea, while coastal stresses position on land.
entries.definitionCN: 指与海运、贸易和法律有关的海洋事务；它强调海上活动，coastal 强调陆上位置。

entries.definition: Of the shore as a place for holidays; it is informal and leisure-oriented, unlike the neutral and technical coastal.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为度假地的海滨；语气随意、偏向休闲，与中性的技术词 coastal 不同。

entries.definition: Situated or working at sea away from the shore; it points outward from the coast rather than lying on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指位于或作业于离岸海上的；它从海岸指向外海，而不是位于岸上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real collocations of the word, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Coastal is the adjective of coast: the noun names the edge, the adjective says what belongs to or sits on it.
normal.cn: coastal 是 coast 的形容词：名词指那条边缘，形容词说明什么属于它或位于它之上。

normal.en: 'Coastal erosion' and 'coastal defence' usually appear together, because defence is the response to erosion.
normal.cn: 海岸侵蚀与海岸防护常常成对出现，因为防护正是对侵蚀的回应。

normal.en: Coastal plain is a standard landform term: low land built up along a shore by sediment.
normal.cn: 海岸平原是标准的地貌术语：由沉积物沿岸堆积成的低地。

normal.en: Coastal waters is the legal and ecological phrase for the belt of sea nearest the land.
normal.cn: 近岸海域是法律与生态上的固定说法，指紧邻陆地的海带。

normal.en: The base verb coast also means to move without engine power, a meaning that grew from sailing along a shore.
normal.cn: 基础动词 coast 还表示不用动力滑行，这个义项由沿岸航行发展而来。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow ribbon of land with fields on one side and white surf on the other, and a road running down its middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄窄的陆带，一侧是农田，一侧是白色浪花，中间一条公路直贯而下。

abstract.en: Picture a town whose harbour, boats and income all face the same direction, out to sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城镇，港口、船只与收入都朝向同一个方向，即外海。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of stone set against the waves, with grass already growing behind it where the sea used to reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一道石墙迎着浪，墙后原本海水到过的地方已经长出了草。

examples.en: The coastal plain is low, flat and built of river sediment.
examples.cn: 海岸平原地势低平，由河流沉积物堆积而成。

examples.en: Coastal waters are warmer and often greener than the open sea.
examples.cn: 近岸海域比外海温暖，颜色也常常更绿。

examples.en: New rules limit building along the coastal strip.
examples.cn: 新规定限制了海岸地带的建设。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「coastal」读似「扣斯头」——「扣」住海岸，「斯头」听着像石头，石头扣在岸上，就是海岸的

root: 拉丁 costa「肋骨、侧面」→ 古法语 coste「肋骨；侧面、岸」→ 中古英语 coast「海岸」→ 加 -al 成 coastal；costa 的更深来源不确定，所拟词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place something on the narrow strip where land meets sea. The adjective first marks the edge itself, then position, habitat, works, people, navigation, rules and finally air, so the coast becomes a place to live on, build on, sail past and govern.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某样东西放在陆海相接的窄带上。这个形容词先标记边缘本身，再依次标记位置、生境、工程、居民、航行、规则，最后是空气，于是海岸成了居住、建造、航行与治理的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow strip of land with the sea on one side and fields on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条窄陆带，一侧是海，另一侧是田野。

branches.en: PLAIN RELATION: the adjective simply marks what belongs to the coast.
branches.cn: 基本关系：形容词只标记什么属于海岸。

branches.en: OCCUPIED EDGE: towns, jobs and incomes sit on the strip.
branches.cn: 有人居住的边缘：城镇、工作与收入都落在这条带上。

branches.en: LIVING EDGE: salt marsh, mangrove and dune form one habitat.
branches.cn: 活的边缘：盐沼、红树林与沙丘构成同一个生境。

branches.en: DEFENDED EDGE: walls and breakwaters try to hold the line.
branches.cn: 设防的边缘：海堤与防波堤试图固定这条线。

branches.en: WORKING EDGE: shipping, planning law and sea air all describe uses of the coast.
branches.cn: 使用中的边缘：航运、规划法规与海风都描述海岸的用途。

intro.en: Coastal is coast plus -al. The family runs from the bare noun coast through the compound coastline and the agent-like coaster to prefixed forms such as intercoastal, which locate activity between or along coasts.
intro.cn: coastal 是 coast 加 -al。其词族从光杆名词 coast，经复合词 coastline 与指物的 coaster，一直到 intercoastal 这类加前缀的形式，用于标明活动发生于海岸之间或沿岸。

latinIntro.en: Latin costa 'rib, side' is the source of coast, and -alis, through French -al, supplies the adjective ending. The anatomical sense survived in costal, which is why the same root yields two very different words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 costa「肋骨、侧面」是 coast 的来源，-alis 经法语 -al 提供形容词词尾。解剖义保留在 costal 中，这正是同一词根产生两个差别很大的词的原因。

items.meaning: the shore; to sail along it
items.example: The coast bends west beyond the headland.
items.exampleCN: 海岸在岬角之外向西弯去。

items.example: A coastal path follows the cliffs.
items.exampleCN: 一条沿海小径贴着悬崖延伸。

items.meaning: the coast seen as a line
items.example: The coastline retreats a metre a year here.
items.exampleCN: 这里的海岸线每年后退一米。

items.meaning: a coastal trading ship; a table mat
items.example: A coaster unloaded salt at the quay.
items.exampleCN: 一艘沿海航船在码头卸下盐。

items.structure: coast + -wise (in the manner or direction of)
items.example: Coastwise traffic keeps the small ports alive.
items.exampleCN: 沿岸航运让这些小港口得以维持。

items.meaning: an agency or person that watches the shore and nearby sea
items.meaningCN: 海岸警卫队；海岸巡防人员
items.example: The coastguard closed the beach during the gale.
items.exampleCN: 大风期间海岸警卫队封闭了海滩。
沿海陆地被排干用于放牧。

items.meaning: running between or linking coasts; also inland between two coasts
items.meaningCN: 沿岸之间的；连接两岸的
items.example: The intercoastal waterway sheltered small boats.
items.exampleCN: 这条沿岸水道为小船提供了避风处。

items.example: The wind turned coastward at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 黄昏时风转向海岸方向。

latinEntries.meaning: a rib; a side or wall

latinEntries.structure: costalis, costale (adjective, third declension; also used in New Latin)
latinEntries.meaning: of the ribs or of a side

definition_zh: adj. 沮丧的；垂头丧气的；气馁的
definition_en: sad and without hope or energy, especially after a setback
core_image: 一个人坐在长椅边，肩塌着、头低着，手里的信纸垂向地面；雨后一只耷拉着翅膀的鸟
scene: 他坐在长椅边上，肩膀塌着，头低低垂向手里的信纸。 He looked downhearted as he read the letter for the third time.
sceneCN: 这里 downhearted 是「垂头丧气的」（第 1 个义项：悲伤、没有希望也没有力气）；句意是他第三遍读那封信时显得垂头丧气。图中可辨识物件：长椅、塌下的肩、低垂的头、垂向地面的信纸。

pos.zh: 沮丧的；垂头丧气的；气馁的

senses.title: Low in spirits
senses.definition: feeling sad and without hope or energy
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）感到悲伤、没有希望也没有力气
senses.example: He felt downhearted after the letter arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 信到了以后他感到沮丧。
senses.why: A person sitting on the edge of a bench with dropped shoulders and head lowered toward a letter.
senses.whyCN: 一个人坐在长椅边上，肩膀塌着，头低垂向手里的信纸。

senses.title: Discouraged by a setback
senses.definition: having lost confidence after a failure or refusal
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）在失败或被拒之后失去信心
senses.example: The team grew downhearted after the third refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 第三次被拒后球队气馁了。
senses.why: A runner stopped at the hurdle that threw him, hands on knees.
senses.whyCN: 一名跑者停在把他绊倒的跨栏前，双手撑着膝盖。

senses.title: Showing low spirits
senses.definition: showing low spirits in the face or manner
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）在神情或举止上显出情绪低落
senses.example: She gave a downhearted smile and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她沮丧地笑了笑，什么也没说。
senses.why: A bird with wings hanging loose after the rain, unable to lift them.
senses.whyCN: 雨后一只翅膀耷拉着的鸟，抬不起来。

intro.en: Downhearted is down plus hearted, with the heart sunk down; English has long placed feeling in the heart, so a heart that has dropped is a spirit that has dropped with it.
intro.cn: downhearted 由 down 加 hearted 组成，心沉了下去；英语长久以来把情感放在心里，所以心一沉，精神也跟着沉。

items.en: Old English heorte means the heart.
items.cn: 古英语 heorte 意为心脏。

items.en: Old English dune means down or downward.
items.cn: 古英语 dune 意为向下。

items.en: Middle English herted means having a heart of a kind.
items.cn: 中古英语 herted 意为有某种心的。

items.en: English builds light-hearted and faint-hearted on the same pattern.
items.cn: 英语按同一格式造出 light-hearted 与 faint-hearted。

items.en: Downhearted is recorded for low spirits after a setback.
items.cn: downhearted 被记录下来，指受挫后情绪低落。

items.en: The word stays informal and describes a temporary mood.
items.cn: 这个词保持非正式色彩，描述一时的情绪。

note.en: Downhearted is a heart sunk down; its look-alikes share the hearted pattern, and its neighbours name nearby shades of low feeling.
note.cn: downhearted 是心沉了下去；形近词共用 hearted 格式，近义词则是低落情绪的邻近层次。

entries.definition: carefree and cheerful
entries.definitionCN: 无忧无虑而快乐的

entries.definition: easily frightened or discouraged
entries.definitionCN: 容易害怕或气馁的

entries.definition: having lost confidence because of something
entries.definitionCN: 因某事而失去信心的

entries.definition: sad and without hope
entries.definitionCN: 悲伤而没有希望的

entries.definition: having lost all hope or courage
entries.definitionCN: 失去全部希望或勇气的

entries.definition: sad, or making one feel sad
entries.definitionCN: 忧郁的；令人忧郁的

dict_mnemonic.text: downhearted ＝ down（向下）＋ heart（心）＋ -ed（有…的）＝「心往下沉的」。英语把情绪放在心里：heart 沉下去，人就没精神、垂头丧气。同格式的还有 lighthearted（心轻＝快活）、fainthearted（心弱＝胆怯）；反义动作是 hearten（使心振作）。

root: 古英语 heorte（心）＋ dune（向下）→ 中古英语 herted（有…心的）→ 现代 downhearted（心沉的＝沮丧的）

sensesIntro.cn: 一颗沉下去的心：信纸前塌下的肩、停在跨栏前的跑者与翅膀耷拉的鸟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person on the edge of a bench with dropped shoulders while a letter hangs toward the ground

intro.en: Downhearted is down plus heart plus -ed; the same -ed pattern builds lighthearted, and the Latin roots anim- and cord- name spirit and heart from another direction.
intro.cn: downhearted 由 down 加 heart 加 -ed 构成；同一个 -ed 格式造出 lighthearted，而拉丁语词根 anim- 与 cord- 从另一个方向指称精神与心。

latinIntro.en: Latin cor means heart, animus spirit and deicere to throw down; tristis means sad.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cor 意为心，animus 意为精神，deicere 意为扔下；tristis 意为悲伤。

definition_zh: 通奸；婚外性行为（尤指一方已婚）
definition_en: sex between a married person and someone who is not that person's husband or wife
core_image: 婚姻围栏上被悄悄打开的一道缺口，只有两个人知道
scene: 老城旅馆的走廊里，一份离婚诉状摊在桌上，理由栏写得极短。 The divorce petition cited adultery as the ground for the marriage's collapse.
sceneCN: 这里 adultery 是「通奸」（第 1 个义项：已婚者与配偶以外的人发生性关系）；句意为这份离婚诉状把通奸列为婚姻破裂的理由。图中可辨识的物件：诉状、钢笔、旅馆房牌。

pos.zh: 通奸；婚外性行为（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -er 构成，指「通奸的男子」
由 adultere 加 -ess 构成的旧式阴性形式，指「通奸的女子」，今多含贬义、渐少用
由词干加 -ous 构成，义为「通奸的；不忠的」

senses.title: The act of sex outside marriage
senses.definition: the act of a married person having sex with someone who is not his or her spouse
senses.definitionCN: 已婚者与配偶以外的人发生性关系的行为
senses.example: The village treated adultery as a private shame and a public fact.
senses.exampleCN: 村里把通奸既当作私下的耻辱，也当作公开的事实。
senses.why: Latin adulterare meant to go to another, and the noun names precisely that act, so this is the plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「走向另一个」，名词命名的正是这一行为，这是最本义的义项。

senses.title: A legal ground for divorce
senses.definition: the act as a recognised reason on which a court may dissolve a marriage
senses.definitionCN: 作为法院可以据以解除婚姻的公认理由的这一行为
senses.example: In this jurisdiction adultery remains a fault-based ground for divorce.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个司法辖区，通奸仍是过错离婚的一项理由。
senses.why: Because marriage is a legal contract, the same act becomes a recognised ground on which the contract may be ended.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻是一份法律契约，因此同一行为成为契约可以据以终止的公认事由。

senses.title: A breach of the marriage vow
senses.definition: the act understood as breaking a promise made before God rather than as a legal fact
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为在神面前毁掉承诺、而非法律事实的这一行为
senses.example: The church called adultery a sin against the wedding vow.
senses.exampleCN: 教会把通奸称为对婚礼誓言的罪。
senses.why: In religious framing the same act is not a legal fact but a broken vow, so the word shifts from deed to sin.
senses.whyCN: 在宗教框架里，同一行为不是法律事实而是被撕毁的誓言，于是这个词从行为转向罪。

senses.title: An accusation brought against someone
senses.definition: the word as a charge that one person lays against another
senses.definitionCN: 一个人加在另一个人头上的这一指控
senses.example: He denied the adultery allegation and demanded proof.
senses.exampleCN: 他否认通奸的指控，并要求拿出证据。
senses.why: Once a name exists for the act, it can be attached to a person as an accusation, and the word enters court language.
senses.whyCN: 行为一旦有了名字，就能安到某个人头上成为指控，这个词于是进入法庭语言。

senses.title: A word weighted by gender
senses.titleCN: 带有性别偏见的旧用法
senses.definition: the historically uneven use of the term, applied far more harshly to wives than to husbands
senses.definitionCN: 这个词在历史上用法不均，对妻子的责难远重于丈夫
senses.example: Old novels punish adulteresses far more severely than adulterers.
senses.exampleCN: 旧小说对通奸女子的惩罚远重于通奸男子。
senses.why: Historically the word was applied far more harshly to women, so its use carries an uneven moral weight.
senses.whyCN: 历史上这个词对女性的责难远重于男性，所以它的使用带着不均衡的道德重量。

senses.title: Betrayal of a pledged loyalty
senses.definition: in figurative use, the breaking of any loyalty or trust that was solemnly pledged
senses.definitionCN: 用于比喻时，指撕毁任何曾郑重立下的忠诚或信任
senses.example: They accused the party of adultery toward its own founding ideals.
senses.exampleCN: 他们指责该政党背叛了自己立党的理想。
senses.why: Any pledged loyalty can be broken in the same shape, so the word extends to betraying a cause or a trust.
senses.whyCN: 任何立誓的忠诚都能以同样的形状被破坏，于是这个词延伸到对事业或信任的背叛。

senses.title: The concealed affair as a plot engine
senses.definition: in literature, the hidden relationship used to drive suspense and revelation
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中，被用来推动悬念与真相揭露的隐秘关系
senses.example: The play turns on adultery discovered through a misplaced letter.
senses.exampleCN: 这出戏靠一封放错地方的信揭出通奸，情节由此转动。
senses.why: A hidden affair is a ready-made engine of suspense, so literature borrows the word for its plots.
senses.whyCN: 隐秘的私情是现成的悬念发动机，文学于是借这个词来推动情节。

senses.title: The public shame of discovery
senses.definition: the scandal that follows when the private act becomes known
senses.definitionCN: 私下的行为被人知道之后随之而来的丑闻
senses.example: The adultery became a scandal that cost him his ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩通奸变成丑闻，使他丢掉了牧师职位。
senses.why: The act only becomes scandal when it is exposed, and the word then names the public noise rather than the private deed.
senses.whyCN: 这一行为只有被揭露才成为丑闻，此时这个词命名的是公开的喧哗，而非私下的行为。

intro.en: Adultery descends from a Latin verb built on alter, the word for other, so its oldest sense is going to someone else.
intro.cn: adultery 源自一个以 alter（另一个）为核心构成的拉丁动词，最古老的意思就是「走向别人」。

items.en: Alter meant the other of two, and it still survives in English alternation and alternative.
items.cn: alter 意为两者中的另一个，至今仍活在英语的 alternation 与 alternative 里。

items.en: Ad plus alter gave adulterare, to go to another and so to commit adultery; it also meant to corrupt.
items.cn: ad 加 alter 构成 adulterare，义为「走向另一个」，因此指通奸，同时也表示「玷污」。

items.en: The noun adulterium named the act itself, and this form is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 名词 adulterium 命名这一行为本身，这一形式正是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French carried the word as avoutrie and later adulterie, with the spelling unsettled for centuries.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带作 avoutrie，后来又作 adulterie，拼写数百年间并不固定。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the fourteenth century, first in religious and legal texts.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪借入这个名词，最早见于宗教与法律文本。

items.en: The modern word keeps both the religious tone and the legal force, though criminal penalties have largely disappeared.
items.cn: 现代英语的这个名词同时保留了宗教语气与法律效力，尽管刑事处罚已大多废除。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same alter family, including one that means to corrupt rather than to stray; the near-meaning group gathers blunter, softer and more clinical labels for the same territory.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 alter 词族的词，其中包括表示「玷污」而非「越界」的一个；近义组收指同一片领域的更直白、更委婉与更临床的说法。

entries.definition: The person who commits the act, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 实施这一行为的人，由施事后缀构成。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the act or the person, formed with -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 描述行为或人的形容词，由 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb but with the idea of corrupting a substance by mixing in something inferior.
entries.definitionCN: 来自同一拉丁动词，但取「掺入次货使物质变劣」之意，与私情无关。

entries.definition: A softer, vaguer word for a romantic relationship outside marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 更委婉含糊的说法，指婚外的感情关系。

entries.definition: A formal term for breaking faith with a partner, broader than the single act.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指对伴侣不忠，范围比单次行为更广。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the same behaviour, carrying no legal or religious weight.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语说法，指同样的行为，不带法律或宗教分量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin alter, the real word family and the legal phrases the noun actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁语 alter、真实的词族，以及这个名词实际构成的短语。

normal.en: Adulterare is ad plus alter: to go to another. The word is built into the meaning.
normal.cn: adulterare 就是 ad 加 alter：走向另一个。词义被写进了构词里。

normal.en: Alter also gives alternative and alter ego, all about a second version.
normal.cn: alter 还给出 alternative 与 alter ego，都与「另一个版本」有关。

normal.en: The family runs adulterer, adulteress and adulterous, so the noun has three ready relatives.
normal.cn: 词族里有 adulterer、adulteress 与 adulterous，这个名词因此有三个现成亲戚。

normal.en: The verb that goes with it is commit, as in commit adultery, not do adultery.
normal.cn: 与它搭配的动词是 commit，说 commit adultery，而不说 do adultery。

normal.en: Legal writing prefers grounds of adultery, a fixed phrase in divorce statutes.
normal.cn: 法律写作偏爱 grounds of adultery，这是离婚法条里的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a second key cut for the same door, made quietly and kept out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象有人悄悄配了同一扇门的第二把钥匙，藏在看不见的地方。

abstract.en: The word names a relationship, but its force comes from the promise it breaks.
abstract.cn: 这个词命名一段关系，但它的力量来自被它撕毁的那个承诺。

abstract.en: Every exposure story repeats the same shape: a private gap, then public light.
abstract.cn: 每个曝光的故事都重复同一个形状：私下的缺口，然后是公开的光。

examples.en: In many countries adultery is no longer a criminal offence.
examples.cn: 在许多国家，通奸已不再是刑事犯罪。

examples.en: The church treated adultery as a breach of the wedding vow.
examples.cn: 教会把通奸视为对婚礼誓言的违背。

examples.en: Novelists have long used adultery to set a plot in motion.
examples.cn: 小说家早就用通奸来推动情节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德尔特里」——德尔另开一扇门：通奸

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ alter（另一个）→ adulterare「走向另一个、玷污」，名词 adulterium 经古法语进入英语，义为通奸。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adultery all turn on one gap opened in a pledged bond: the act itself, its legal force, its religious weight, the charge, the uneven blame, the figurative betrayal, the literary engine and the public scandal.
sensesIntro.cn: adultery 的八个义项都围绕一个在誓约上打开的缺口：行为本身、法律效力、宗教重量、指控、不均的责难、比喻性的背叛、文学里的情节引擎，以及公开的丑闻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gap quietly opened in the fence around a marriage.
core.cn: 核心意象：婚姻围栏上被悄悄打开的一道缺口。

branches.en: THE DEED LINE: the act and the broken vow are two readings of the same private step.
branches.cn: 行为线：行为与被撕毁的誓言，是对同一个私下举动的两种读法。

branches.en: THE COURT LINE: the deed becomes a ground and then a charge once lawyers take it up.
branches.cn: 法庭线：一旦律师介入，行为先成为事由，再成为指控。

branches.en: THE BLAME LINE: the same word has weighed more heavily on wives than on husbands.
branches.cn: 责难线：同一个词压在妻子身上的分量历来重于丈夫。

branches.en: THE STORY LINE: the shape of a broken pledge can be borrowed for causes and for plots.
branches.cn: 故事线：被毁誓约的形状可以被借去说事业，也可以被借去写情节。

branches.en: THE SCANDAL LINE: exposure turns the private gap into public noise.
branches.cn: 丑闻线：曝光把私下的缺口变成公开的喧哗。

intro.en: Adultery is a Latin noun in -ium built on the verb adulterare, whose core is alter, the other; English keeps the stem and adds English agent and adjective endings.
intro.cn: adultery 是以 -ium 结尾的拉丁名词，建于动词 adulterare 之上，其核心是 alter（另一个）；英语保留词干，并加上英语的施事与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Alter, adulterare and adulterium are all attested in Latin, so nothing here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: alter、adulterare 与 adulterium 在拉丁语中均有文献，此处没有构拟形式。

items.example: It turns alter into a motion toward the other.
items.exampleCN: 它把 alter 变成「朝另一个而去」的动作。

items.example: It is the semantic heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词的意义核心。

items.meaning: to commit adultery, also to corrupt
items.example: Its noun is the source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它的名词形式是英语词的来源。

items.example: It carries the Latin noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁名词带入英语。

items.example: It forms the old word adulteress.

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -er 构成，义为「通奸的男子」
由词干加 -ess 构成的旧式阴性形式，义为「通奸的女子」
由词干加 -ous 构成，义为「通奸的；不忠的」

definition_zh: 亚种；种以下的分类等级
definition_en: a group of populations within a species that differ from other populations, usually in geography or form
core_image: 同一片大陆上被山脉隔开的两群同类，毛色深浅不同，却仍能互交
scene: 博物馆把来自两座相隔很远的岛屿的甲虫标本定为同一物种下的两个不同亚种。 The museum assigned beetle specimens from two distant islands to two different subspecies of the same species.
sceneCN: 这里 subspecies 是「亚种」（第 1 个义项：种之下的分类等级）；句意：博物馆把来自两座相隔很远岛屿的甲虫标本，定为同一物种下的两个不同亚种。

pos.zh: 亚种（单复数同形，略作 subsp. 或 ssp.）

derivatives.zh: 变种（植物分类中低于亚种的等级）
变型（植物分类中的最低等级）

senses.title: A rank below species
senses.definition: the taxonomic rank immediately below species, grouping populations that share a distinct set of features
senses.definitionCN: 紧接在物种之下的分类阶元，把具有一组独特性状的群体聚合起来
senses.example: The museum assigned the two island beetles to different subspecies.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把两座岛上的甲虫定为不同的亚种。
senses.why: Sub- 'under' plus species makes the rank literal: the same kind, divided one step further down.
senses.whyCN: sub-「在下」加 species 把阶元关系写得很直白：同一个种，再往下分一级。

senses.title: A geographical race
senses.definition: a set of populations separated by geography that have come to differ in colour, size or behaviour while remaining interfertile
senses.definitionCN: 因地理分隔而在毛色、体型或行为上出现差异、却仍能互交的群体
senses.example: The northern subspecies is darker and slightly smaller.
senses.exampleCN: 北方的亚种颜色更深，体型略小。
senses.why: Most subspecies begin as geography: a barrier stops gene flow long enough for local features to accumulate, but not long enough to block breeding.
senses.whyCN: 多数亚种起于地理：屏障阻断基因流的时间足以让地方特征积累，却还不足以阻断繁殖。

senses.title: The trinomial name
senses.definition: the three-part scientific name that adds a subspecies epithet to the binomial, as in Homo sapiens sapiens
senses.definitionCN: 在双名之后再加一个亚种加词的三段式学名，如智人的指名亚种
senses.example: The trinomial name repeats the species epithet for the nominate subspecies.
senses.exampleCN: 指名亚种的名称会把种加词重复一遍。
senses.why: Because a subspecies sits below a species, its name needs one more slot; the trinomial is that slot, and it is written in italics with the rank not capitalized.
senses.whyCN: 由于亚种位于种之下，其名称需要多一个位置；三名法就是那个位置，书写时用斜体且亚种加词不大写。

senses.title: Nomenclatural rules and abbreviations
senses.definition: the set of rules that govern valid subspecies names, together with the abbreviations subsp. and ssp. used in catalogs
senses.definitionCN: 管理亚种名称有效性的规则，以及标本目录中使用的缩写 subsp. 与 ssp.
senses.example: The label reads subsp. borealis, following the code.
senses.exampleCN: 标签按法规写作 subsp. borealis。
senses.why: Codes exist so that a name means the same thing in every collection; the abbreviation marks the rank without spelling it out, which saves space on a label.
senses.whyCN: 法规的存在是为了让一个名称在每一份收藏中都指同一事物；缩写在不写出全称的情况下标出阶元，可节省标签空间。

senses.title: Plural identical to singular
senses.definition: the form subspecies used for both one and several, following the Latin pattern of species
senses.definitionCN: 一个与多个都写作 subspecies，沿用 species 的拉丁模式
senses.example: Two subspecies were recognized, and one subspecies was newly described.
senses.exampleCN: 识别出两个亚种，其中一个为新描述。
senses.why: Latin species had an unchanging plural, and the compound keeps it: only the verb or a numeral shows whether the word is singular.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 species 的复数不变，这个复合词沿用了这一点：只有动词或数词能表明该词是单数还是复数。

senses.title: Subspecies and variety in botany
senses.titleCN: 植物学中亚种与变种的分别
senses.definition: in botanical nomenclature, a rank that ranks above variety and below species, used for geographically distinct wild populations
senses.definitionCN: 植物命名法中位于变种之上、物种之下、用于地理上独立的野生群体的等级
senses.example: Botanists treat the coastal form as a subspecies, not a variety.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把海岸类型处理为亚种，而不是变种。
senses.why: Botany needed finer steps than zoology, so it placed variety and forma below subspecies; the two words are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要比动物学更细的台阶，于是在亚种之下再设变种与变型；这两个词不能互换。

senses.title: A unit in conservation planning
senses.definition: a population unit recognized in conservation because its distinct traits would be lost if it disappeared
senses.definitionCN: 因其独特性状一旦消失就会丧失、而在保护工作中被承认的群体单元
senses.example: Managers list the island subspecies as a priority for captive breeding.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者把这个岛屿亚种列为圈养繁殖的优先对象。
senses.why: Conservation works with units it can act on; a named subspecies gives a legal and practical handle even when the biological status is debated.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作需要可施加行动的单元；即使生物学地位仍有争议，一个有名称的亚种也提供了法律与实践上的抓手。

senses.title: Subspecies in microbiology
senses.definition: a formal rank used for bacterial strains that differ in antigenic or biochemical characters within one species
senses.definitionCN: 用于同一物种内抗原或生化性状不同的菌株的正式等级
senses.example: The culture was classified as a subspecies of the common gut bacterium.
senses.exampleCN: 该培养物被定为常见肠道细菌的一个亚种。
senses.why: Microbiology adopted the rank because bacterial species can be very broad; subspecies gives a legal name to a recognizable strain without raising it to species.
senses.whyCN: 微生物学采用这个等级，因为细菌的种可以定得很宽；亚种给了可辨识菌株一个正式名称，而无需把它提升为种。

senses.title: The rank as a matter of judgement
senses.titleCN: 作为判断问题的亚种划分
senses.definition: a classification that depends on how much difference taxonomists decide is enough, and therefore often revised
senses.definitionCN: 取决于分类学家认定差异足够大与否、因而常被修订的分类处理
senses.example: The two subspecies were later merged when the boundary proved continuous.
senses.exampleCN: 当界线被证明是连续的，这两个亚种后来被合并。
senses.why: Subspecies is the rank most exposed to disagreement, since the line between a local form and a full species is drawn by judgement rather than by a single test.
senses.whyCN: 亚种是最容易引起分歧的阶元，因为地方类型与完整物种之间的界线靠判断划定，而不是靠单一判据。

intro.en: Subspecies is a modern scientific compound: Latin sub- 'under' fastened to species. It was coined for taxonomy rather than inherited from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subspecies 是近代科学复合词：拉丁前缀 sub-「在下」加 species，为分类学而造，并非从拉丁语整体继承。年代为约数。

items.en: Sub- meant 'under, below' and was already productive in Latin compounds such as subicere and substructio.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下、低于」，在拉丁复合词中已很能产，如 subicere 与 substructio。

items.en: Species meant 'appearance, kind' and served as the basic logical class before it became a biological rank.
items.cn: species 意为「外观、种类」，在成为生物阶元之前是基本的逻辑类别。

items.en: As ranks multiplied, naturalists needed a step between the broad species of the day and the local form, and the compound was available.
items.cn: 随着阶元增多，博物学者需要在当时较宽的种与地方类型之间加一级，而这个复合形式正好可用。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century nomenclature codes fixed the trinomial and the abbreviations subsp. and ssp.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪的命名法规确定了三名法以及 subsp.、ssp. 两种缩写。

items.en: Molecular data have forced many subspecies to be merged or raised, so the rank is now more often a provisional judgement than a settled fact.
items.cn: 分子数据迫使许多亚种被合并或提升，因此这个阶元如今更像临时判断，而非定论。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of subspecies as a formal rank is not fixed here, and no classical Latin noun subspecies is attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：subspecies 作为正式阶元的最早使用年份此处无法确定；古典拉丁语中并无 subspecies 这一名词。

note.en: Group one separates ranks and names that sit near subspecies; group two compares the words for local forms at different depths.
note.cn: 第一组区分与亚种相邻的阶元与名称；第二组比较不同深度的「地方类型」用词。

entries.definition: The basic rank itself: one step up from subspecies, and the unit that the trinomial's second word names.
entries.definitionCN: 基本阶元本身：比亚种高一级，也是三名法中第二个词所命名的单位。

entries.definition: Relating to a subspecies, as in subspecific epithet. It is the adjective, while subspecies is the rank noun.
entries.definitionCN: 与亚种有关的，如亚种加词。它是形容词，subspecies 是阶元名词。

entries.definition: A group of closely related species treated together, the opposite direction from subspecies.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干近缘物种合并看待的类群，方向与亚种相反。

entries.definition: A mathematical space contained in another space. Sub- is shared, but species is not the source; it is built on space.
entries.definitionCN: 包含于另一空间的数学空间。共用了 sub-，但词源不是 species，而是建立在 space 之上。

entries.definition: In botany, a rank below subspecies for a minor wild variant; in everyday use, simply a sort or kind.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学中位于亚种之下、用于细微野生变异的等级；日常则泛指种类。

entries.definition: A loosely used term for a geographically distinct breeding group; it has no fixed rank in the codes.
entries.definitionCN: 对地理上独立的繁殖群体的宽松称呼；在命名法规中没有固定阶元。

entries.definition: A genetically distinct line maintained in the laboratory or in breeding, finer and less formal than a subspecies.
entries.definitionCN: 实验室或育种中保持的遗传独立品系，比亚种更细、更不正式。

entries.definition: In botany, forma, a minor morphological variant below variety; the smallest recognized step.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学中的变型，位于变种之下、最小的可识别台阶。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sub- 'under' plus species: one step below the basic rank.
normal.cn: sub-「在下」加 species：基本阶元之下的一级。

normal.en: The trinomial adds a third word: genus, species, subspecies.
normal.cn: 三名法再加一个词：属名、种名、亚种名。

normal.en: The nomination subspecies repeats the species epithet, which makes it easy to spot in a name.
normal.cn: 指名亚种会重复种加词，因此在名称里一眼可辨。

normal.en: Botany puts variety and forma below subspecies, so the ranks are ordered rather than interchangeable.
normal.cn: 植物学把变种与变型放在亚种之下，因此这些阶元有先后，不能互换。

normal.en: Labels abbreviate the rank as subsp. or ssp. to save space.
normal.cn: 标签把阶元缩写成 subsp. 或 ssp. 以节省空间。

abstract.en: Picture a country with provinces: still one country, but each province has its own flag.
abstract.cn: 想象一个有省份的国家：仍是一个国家，但每省有自己的旗。

abstract.en: Picture two editions of one book, differing in a chapter or two but readable as the same work.
abstract.cn: 想象同一本书的两个版本，相差一两章，却仍可读作同一部作品。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a map by a committee, revised at the next meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象一条由委员会在地图上划出的线，下次会议又被修订。

examples.en: The desert subspecies nests earlier than the coastal one.
examples.cn: 沙漠亚种比海岸亚种更早筑巢。

examples.en: Codes require the subspecies epithet to be lower-case even when it honours a place.
examples.cn: 法规要求亚种加词即使纪念地名也用小写。

examples.en: A recent review sank three subspecies into one on genetic evidence.
examples.cn: 最近一篇综述依据遗传证据把三个亚种合并为一个。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sub 在下 + species 物种」——物种底下的那一层 → subspecies 亚种

root: 拉丁 sub-「在下」+ species「物种」；近代分类学为表示种下阶元而造的复合词，古典拉丁语无此名词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of subspecies follow the rank from its formal position downward: a step below species, a geographic race, a three-word name, a set of naming rules, an unchanging plural, a botanical neighbour, a conservation unit, a microbiological label and finally a judgement that keeps being revised.
sensesIntro.cn: subspecies 的九个义项沿着这个阶元向下展开：种下的一级、地理宗、三名式名称、命名规则、不变的复数、植物学中的邻级、保护单元、微生物学标签，最后是一个不断被修订的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one kind divided by a map line that is real enough to name but not deep enough to split.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个种类被一条地图上的线分开，足以命名，却不足以分裂。

branches.en: THE RANK AND ITS ORIGIN: a step below species, usually produced by geography.
branches.cn: 阶元与来源：种下的一级，通常由地理分隔产生。

branches.en: THE NAME: three words, a code of rules, and a plural that never changes form.
branches.cn: 名称：三个词、一套规则、一个永不改变形式的复数。

branches.en: BOTANICAL ORDER: variety and forma sit still lower, so the ranks form a ladder.
branches.cn: 植物学的次序：变种与变型还在更低处，阶元因此形成梯子。

branches.en: APPLIED USES: conservation acts on the named unit, microbiology uses it for strains.
branches.cn: 应用：保护工作作用于有名称的单元，微生物学用它标记菌株。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: how much difference is enough is decided, not measured.
branches.cn: 判断：差异要多大才算够，是决定的，不是测出来的。

intro.en: Subspecies is built from two Latin pieces but is itself a modern scientific word; the pieces are transparent even though the compound is recent.
intro.cn: subspecies 由两个拉丁成分构成，但本身是近代科学词；复合词虽新，成分却透明。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- yields submarine, subsoil and subordinate; species yields species, subspecies and speciation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sub- 衍生 submarine、subsoil、subordinate；species 衍生 species、subspecies、speciation。

items.example: Sub- places the rank one step lower.
items.exampleCN: sub- 把这个阶元放到低一级的位置。

items.example: Species supplies the rank that is being divided.
items.exampleCN: species 提供被再分的那个阶元。

items.example: The island form is treated as a subspecies.
items.exampleCN: 岛上的类型被处理为亚种。

items.example: A subspecific name follows the trinomial.
Older catalogs prefer ssp. to subsp.
items.exampleCN: 较老的目录更常用 ssp. 而非 subsp.。

items.meaning: a group of closely related species
items.example: The superspecies is split into three geographical species.
items.exampleCN: 这个超种被分成三个地理物种。
植物学把变种排在亚种之下。

definition_zh: 麻醉剂；麻醉药；（形容词）麻醉的；使失去感觉的
definition_en: a substance that causes loss of sensation; relating to or causing anesthesia
core_image: 一支针管让疼痛沉睡：身体还在，感觉先离场
scene: 牙医举起注射器，病人闭上眼睛。 The dentist gave her an anesthetic before pulling the wisdom tooth.
sceneCN: 这里 anesthetic 是「麻醉剂」（第 1 个义项：使失去感觉的物质）；句意为：牙医在拔智齿前给她注射了麻醉剂。

pos.zh: 麻醉剂；麻醉药
麻醉的；使麻木的

derivatives.zh: anesthetic 的状态名词，义为「麻醉；麻木」

senses.title: A drug causing loss of sensation
senses.definition: a substance given to a patient to prevent pain during medical procedures
senses.definitionCN: 给病人使用以在医疗过程中防止疼痛的物质
senses.example: The surgeon chose a general anesthetic for the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生为这次手术选择了全身麻醉剂。
senses.why: The Greek root means without sensation, so the noun names the thing that removes feeling.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根义为「没有感觉」，名词即指去除感觉之物。

senses.title: Loss of feeling produced by a drug
senses.definition: the state of temporary lost sensation produced by such a substance
senses.definitionCN: 此类物质造成的暂时性感觉丧失状态
senses.example: She was under anesthetic for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她在麻醉状态下度过了三小时。
senses.why: The drug and the state it produces share one word, as cause and effect merge.
senses.whyCN: 药物与其产生的状态共用一词，因果合于一体。

senses.title: Relating to anesthesia
senses.definition: connected with or used in anesthesia
senses.definitionCN: 与麻醉相关或用于麻醉的
senses.example: Anesthetic drugs require careful dosing.
senses.exampleCN: 麻醉药物需要精确控制剂量。
senses.why: Once the noun existed, the adjective naturally described everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 名词确立后，形容词自然用于描述与之相关的一切。

senses.title: Numbed or dulled in feeling
senses.definition: unable to feel physical sensation in part or all of the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体局部或全部无法感受物理刺激
senses.example: His fingers stayed anesthetic after the cold night.
senses.exampleCN: 寒冷一夜之后，他的手指依然麻木。
senses.why: Sensation removed by cold feels like sensation removed by a drug, so the adjective spread.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷夺走感觉如同药物夺走感觉，形容词因此扩散使用。

senses.title: Emotionally deadening
senses.titleCN: （比喻）令人麻木的；麻痹情感的
senses.definition: dulling emotional response or awareness
senses.definitionCN: 使情感反应或意识变得迟钝
senses.example: The constant bad news had an anesthetic effect on the public.
senses.exampleCN: 接连的坏消息对公众产生了麻醉般的效果。
senses.why: Loss of feeling extends from the skin to the heart, from body to mind.
senses.whyCN: 「失去感觉」从皮肤延伸到内心，从身体扩展到心灵。

senses.title: A local numbing agent
senses.definition: an anesthetic applied to one small area rather than the whole body
senses.definitionCN: 只作用于身体局部而非全身的麻醉剂
senses.example: The cut was stitched with a local anesthetic only.
senses.exampleCN: 缝 合伤口时只用了局部麻醉剂。
senses.why: Sensation can be switched off in one room of the body while the rest stays awake.
senses.whyCN: 感觉可以在身体的「一个房间」被关闭，而其余部分保持清醒。

senses.title: A general anesthetic: full unconsciousness
senses.definition: an anesthetic that puts the whole body and mind to sleep for surgery
senses.definitionCN: 使全身与意识进入睡眠以施行手术的麻醉剂
senses.example: General anesthetics carry higher risks than local ones.
senses.exampleCN: 全身麻醉剂比局部麻醉风险更高。
senses.why: When the whole house sleeps, the anesthesia is general rather than local.
senses.whyCN: 当整座「房子」都睡着，麻醉便是全身性而非局部性。

senses.title: An anesthetic to something: a soothing distraction
senses.definition: something that numbs worry or pain without solving it
senses.definitionCN: 麻痹忧虑或痛苦而不解决问题的事物
senses.example: Entertainment became an anesthetic to his anxiety.
senses.exampleCN: 娱乐成了麻痹他焦虑的麻醉剂。
senses.why: What quiets pain temporarily becomes, in metaphor, any numbing comfort.
senses.whyCN: 能暂时止痛之物，在比喻中泛化为一切麻木性的慰藉。

intro.en: Anesthetic is a modern scientific coinage built from Greek parts that say exactly what it does: no sensation.
intro.cn: anesthetic 是用希腊语部件拼装的现代科学造词，字面即「没有感觉」。

items.en: The root *dhē- meant to set or place, giving Greek aisthēsis, sensation, through a sense of perceiving what is presented.
items.cn: 原始印欧词根 *dhē- 义为「放置」，经由「感知所呈现之物」一义发展出希腊语 aisthēsis（感觉）。一般认为此联系成立。

items.en: Anaisthēsia meant insensibility, from ana- (without) plus aisthēsis (sensation).
items.cn: 希腊语 anaisthēsia 意为「无感觉」，由 ana-（无）加 aisthēsis（感觉）构成。

items.en: Oliver Wendell Holmes coined anesthesia in 1846, the year ether anesthesia was first publicly demonstrated.
items.cn: 1846 年乙醚麻醉首次公开展示，同年奥利弗·温德尔·霍姆斯创造了 anesthesia 一词。

items.en: The agent noun anesthetic quickly followed, and British spelling kept the extra a as anaesthetic.
items.cn: 表 agent 的 anesthetic 随之出现；英式拼写保留多余的 a，作 anaesthetic。

items.en: Today anesthetic names the drugs, the state, and, as an adjective, everything numbing.
items.cn: 如今 anesthetic 既指麻醉药物与状态，作形容词也指一切令人麻木之物。

note.en: Grouped by shared Greek roots and by nearby meanings of numbing and sensation.
note.cn: 按共享的希腊词根与「麻痹、感觉」的近义关系分组。

entries.definition: the state of lost sensation; the source noun of anesthetic
entries.definitionCN: 感觉丧失状态，anesthetic 的源名词，同根

entries.definition: relating to beauty or artistic taste
entries.definitionCN: 审美的；美学的，与 anesthetic 只是部分拼写相近，词根同出 aisthēsis 但词义不同

entries.definition: experiencing one sense through another, as hearing colors
entries.definitionCN: 联觉的（如听见颜色），共享 aisthēsis 词根

entries.definition: a drug that relieves pain without full loss of sensation
entries.definitionCN: 止痛药，止痛但不完全消除感觉

entries.definition: a drug that calms rather than numbs
entries.definitionCN: 镇静剂，作用是安抚而非消除感觉

entries.definition: causing loss of physical or emotional feeling
entries.definitionCN: 使麻木的，日常用语的近义表达

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek roots ana- and aisthēsis.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的希腊词根 ana- 与 aisthēsis。

normal.en: ana- = without; aisthēsis = sensation; so anesthetic is literally without-sensation.
normal.cn: ana- 表「无」，aisthēsis 表「感觉」，anesthetic 字面即「无感觉」。

normal.en: Same root: esthetic deals with what the senses perceive, anesthetic removes perception.
normal.cn: 同根词：esthetic 处理感官所感知之物，anesthetic 则移除感知。

normal.en: Synesthesia joins senses, anesthesia cuts them off.
normal.cn: synesthesia（联觉）让感官相连，anesthesia 则切断感官。

normal.en: British spelling anaesthetic keeps two a's, like anaemia keeps its second a.
normal.cn: 英式拼写 anaesthetic 有两个 a，与 anaemia 的双 a 一致。

normal.en: The family grows: anesthetic → anesthetize → anesthetist.
normal.cn: 词族可延伸：anesthetic → anesthetize（使麻醉）→ anesthetist（麻醉师）。

abstract.en: Picture feeling draining out of your arm like water from a leaking tube.
abstract.cn: 想象感觉像水从漏管中一样从手臂里流走。

abstract.en: See a dimmer switch turning sensation down to zero before an operation.
abstract.cn: 想象手术前有一个调光开关把「感觉」一路调到零。

abstract.en: Feel cotton wrapping your mind: soft, distant, unable to register pain.
abstract.cn: 感受棉花裹住头脑：柔软、遥远、无法感知疼痛。

examples.en: The operation was performed under a general anesthetic.
examples.cn: 手术在全身麻醉下进行。

examples.en: Apply the anesthetic cream before the injection.
examples.cn: 注射前先涂麻醉药膏。

examples.en: The news had an anesthetic effect on the exhausted city.
examples.cn: 消息对精疲力竭的城市产生了麻木般的效果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺没感觉」——打了麻醉针，俺没感觉了，正好对应 anesthetic 的字面义「无感觉」。

root: 希腊语 ana-（无）+ aisthēsis（感觉，源自一般认为的印欧词根 *dhē-「放置」）→ 希腊语 anaisthēsia「无感觉」→ 1846 年英语 anesthesia → anesthetic。词根确凿，造词年代明确。

sensesIntro.en: From the Greek idea of without sensation, the word covers the drug, the state, the adjective field of numbing, and two metaphorical senses of emotional deadening.
sensesIntro.cn: 从希腊语「无感觉」的概念出发，词义覆盖药物、状态、麻木类形容词用法，以及两个情感麻痹的比喻义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sensation switched off like a light
core.cn: 核心意象：感觉像灯一样被关掉

branches.en: the agents that remove feeling
branches.cn: 去除感觉的药剂（局部与全身）

branches.en: the state of lost sensation
branches.cn: 感觉丧失的状态

branches.en: the adjective field around numbing
branches.cn: 麻木周围的形容词用法

branches.en: metaphorical deadening of emotion
branches.cn: 情感麻痹的比喻用法

branches.en: from body numbness to mind numbness
branches.cn: 从身体麻木到心灵麻木

intro.en: Anesthetic is a transparent compound of Greek prefix, root, and suffix, with a wide family of sensation words.
intro.cn: anesthetic 由希腊前缀、词根、后缀透明拼成，并有一个庞大的「感觉」词族。

latinIntro.en: Though built from Greek, the family lives alongside Latin-derived sensation words in English.
latinIntro.cn: 尽管由希腊语构成，这个词族在英语中与拉丁来源的感觉类词并存。

items.example: Aesthetics is the philosophy of perception and beauty.
items.exampleCN: aesthetics 是关于知觉与美的哲学。

items.meaning: relating to; of the nature of
items.example: Synthetic and energetic share this suffix shape.
items.exampleCN: synthetic 与 energetic 有类似后缀形态。

items.example: Synesthesia joins two senses into one experience.
items.exampleCN: synesthesia 将两种感觉合并为一种体验。

items.meaning: a person who does or practices

items.example: Hyperesthesia makes light touch feel painful.
items.exampleCN: 感觉过敏使轻微触碰也感到疼痛。
